.github/copilot-instructions.md:
# GitHub Copilot Instructions — projects-orchestrator

Canonical agent rules: [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) | Workflow: [.agents/project-init.md](../.agents/project-init.md)

## Issue & project tracking

- Tracking system: **GitHub Projects** (kanban board) + **GitHub Issues** (tickets)
- Create issues: load the `create-issue` skill and use `.agents/scripts/create-issue.sh`; it handles metadata gathering, priority labels, and acceptance criteria
- Board cards move automatically via `board-automation.yml` — no manual updates needed
- Use a dedicated branch for each issue; format it as `<issue_type>/<project_abbr>-<issue_number>-<slug>`, e.g. `feat/PI-42-add-auth`; no direct commits to `main`
- Issue and PR names use a project key: `<PROJECT-KEY>-<issue-number>`, e.g. `PI-42`
- PR titles must follow Conventional Commits with the issue key as scope: `type(PROJECT-123): description` where type ∈ {feat, fix, chore, docs, test}, e.g. `feat(PI-42): Add OAuth login`
- For small no-issue PRs omit the scope: `type: description`, e.g. `fix: Fix typo`
- PR body must still include the GitHub numeric reference `Closes #N` — auto-closes issue and moves board card to Done on merge (skip for no-issue PRs)
- Draft PRs are opened immediately when work starts, not when done
- When asked to push/finish a PR, load the `github-workflow` skill for the full lifecycle and review-cycle protocol.
- No direct commits to `main`
- Branch model: single-trunk — feature PRs target `main` and squash-merge. Environments are a deploy-time concern, not a branching concern.

## Key rules

- Test-first for design (a new interface or fix); then prove each guard can fail — break what it checks, watch it fail, then restore
- No secrets in code — use `os.environ` or `.env` (gitignored)
- `just lint` must pass before closing a task (`just --list` shows all recipes)
- Prefer deterministic bash/python over LLM calls for hooks and scripts
- Permanent decisions → `.agents/docs/decisions/`; reusable facts → `.agents/memory/`
.github/hooks/commit-msg:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# commit-msg hook: validate commit message format before push.
# Install: run .agents/scripts/install-hooks.sh once after cloning (manual step).
#
# Canonical format (Conventional Commits, ADR-006):
#   feat(PI-42): Add OAuth login        (issue-linked — key as scope)
#   fix: Fix typo in README             (no linked issue)
#   feat(PI-9)!: Drop python 3.10       (breaking change)
#
# Legacy format still accepted during transition:
#   [PI-42][feat] Add OAuth login
#   [nojira][fix] Fix typo in README
#
# Any uppercase project key works: PI-, APP-, API-, WEB-, etc.
# Types: feat  fix  chore  docs  test

MSG=$(cat "$1")

# Allow merge commits, fixups, reverts, and WIP
if echo "$MSG" | grep -qE '^(Merge|Revert|fixup!|squash!|WIP)'; then
  exit 0
fi

# Allow GitHub co-author trailers (multi-line commits)
FIRST_LINE=$(echo "$MSG" | head -1)

# Conventional Commits with optional issue-key scope (canonical)
if echo "$FIRST_LINE" | grep -qE '^(feat|fix|chore|docs|test)(\([A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,9}-[0-9]+\))?!?: .+'; then
  exit 0
fi

# Legacy bracket format (transition)
if echo "$FIRST_LINE" | grep -qE '^\[([A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,9}-[0-9]+|nojira)\]\[(feat|fix|chore|docs|test)\] .+'; then
  exit 0
fi

echo "" >&2
echo "ERROR: commit message format invalid." >&2
echo "" >&2
echo "Required: <type>(<PROJECT>-<n>): Short description" >&2
echo "      or: <type>: Short description        (no linked issue)" >&2
echo "" >&2
echo "Types: feat  fix  chore  docs  test" >&2
echo "" >&2
echo "Examples:" >&2
echo "  feat(PI-42): Add OAuth login" >&2
echo "  fix(APP-99): Handle null pointer in auth" >&2
echo "  chore: Bump dev dependency" >&2
echo "" >&2
echo "Your message: $FIRST_LINE" >&2
echo "" >&2
exit 1
.github/hooks/pre-commit:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pre-commit hook (ADR-007). Two gates, fastest-feedback-first:
#   1. Lint: run `just lint` so a human committing from a terminal/IDE is held
#      to the SAME static gate CI runs (ruff + shfmt + shellcheck). The Claude
#      pre-commit-gate.sh only fires for agent-driven commits; this catches
#      everyone. Fail-CLOSED when the tooling is present (block the commit,
#      bypassable with `git commit --no-verify`); fail-open when `just`/the
#      recipe is absent so a fresh clone without the toolchain still commits.
#   2. Secrets: scan staged changes with gitleaks. Fail-OPEN if gitleaks is
#      missing — the CI secret-scan job is the hard backstop.
# Install: .agents/scripts/install-hooks.sh

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"

# 1. Lint gate — same command surface as CI and the agent commit gate (PI-139).
if command -v just >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$REPO_ROOT/justfile" ] &&
  (cd "$REPO_ROOT" && just --show lint >/dev/null 2>&1); then
  # Lint exactly the STAGED snapshot, not the working tree: otherwise an unstaged
  # fix could mask a staged lint error (or unstaged WIP could fail a clean
  # commit). Temporarily strip unstaged tracked changes with a saved patch — NOT
  # `git stash`, whose pop merges and leaves conflict markers when the same file
  # is both staged and unstaged. A patch reverse/forward is conflict-free here
  # because `just lint` is read-only. A trap always restores; if the tree can't
  # be isolated safely (e.g. binary diffs, apply failure), fall back to linting
  # the worktree rather than risk touching it. No unstaged changes → the worktree
  # already equals the index, so skip the dance entirely.
  #
  # `git apply` is NOT atomic (PI-811): on a fatal error it can modify and delete
  # files and *then* exit non-zero. So a non-zero exit does NOT mean "nothing was
  # touched" — treating it as such destroyed uncommitted work on every commit.
  # Three independent guards, outermost first:
  #
  #   1. Refuse to isolate at all when the diff cannot survive an apply (see
  #      _isolable). This is the guard that actually catches the reported cases;
  #      the two obvious alternatives do NOT, and both were tried:
  #        - `git apply -R --check` returns 0 on these diffs, and the real apply
  #          then wrecks the tree. The dry run cannot be relied on.
  #        - git reports the replacement as a plain delete, not a type change,
  #          so `--diff-filter=T` comes back empty.
  #   2. Dry-run anyway (`--check` writes nothing) for the classes it does catch.
  #   3. Install the restore trap BEFORE the real apply, never after — a partial
  #      revert with no trap has nothing to undo it.
  #
  # And never delete the patch on a failure path: it is the only copy of the
  # user's unstaged work.
  #
  # Every git call below is anchored with `-C "$REPO_ROOT"`, and paths from
  # `git diff` are resolved against it. `git diff` emits root-relative paths and
  # `git apply` interprets them relative to CWD — git itself runs hooks from the
  # worktree root, but nothing here should depend on that, and the directory
  # probe in _isolable would silently stop detecting anything if it did.
  _isolable() {
    # A path in the diff that is now a DIRECTORY in the worktree: `git apply`
    # cannot write a file where a directory stands, and it fails only *after*
    # deleting earlier files in the patch. Covers both replacement shapes — a
    # tracked symlink swapped for a dir (what `project-init upgrade` does to
    # `.claude`) AND a tracked regular file swapped for a dir; the file's mode
    # stays 100644, so mode-sniffing alone would miss the second entirely.
    local _f
    while IFS= read -r -d '' _f; do
      if [ -d "$REPO_ROOT/$_f" ]; then
        return 1
      fi
    done < <(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" diff --name-only -z 2>/dev/null)
    # Symlinks and gitlinks are fragile under apply even without a dir clash.
    ! git -C "$REPO_ROOT" diff --raw 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1, $2}' |
      grep -qE '120000|160000'
  }
  _patch=""
  _restore() {
    [ -n "$_patch" ] || return 0
    if git -C "$REPO_ROOT" apply --whitespace=nowarn "$_patch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      rm -f "$_patch"
      _patch=""
      return 0
    fi
    # Restore failed — the worktree may be missing unstaged work. Never swallow
    # this, and never `rm` the patch: it is the only way back.
    echo "" >&2
    echo "❌ pre-commit: could NOT restore your unstaged changes." >&2
    echo "   Your working tree may be missing uncommitted work. The patch that" >&2
    echo "   restores it has been kept:" >&2
    echo "" >&2
    echo "     $_patch" >&2
    echo "" >&2
    echo "   Recover with (the patch has repo-root-relative paths, so -C matters):" >&2
    echo "     git -C '$REPO_ROOT' apply --whitespace=nowarn '$_patch'" >&2
    _patch=""
    exit 1
  }
  if ! git -C "$REPO_ROOT" diff --quiet 2>/dev/null; then
    _p="$(mktemp)"
    if _isolable && git -C "$REPO_ROOT" diff --binary --no-color >"$_p" 2>/dev/null &&
      git -C "$REPO_ROOT" apply -R --check --whitespace=nowarn "$_p" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      _patch="$_p"
      trap _restore EXIT
      if ! git -C "$REPO_ROOT" apply -R --whitespace=nowarn "$_p" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        # --check passed but the apply still broke partway: the tree may be
        # half-reverted. _restore puts it back, and shouts if it cannot.
        _restore
        trap - EXIT
        echo "❌ pre-commit: could not isolate the staged snapshot; nothing was committed." >&2
        exit 1
      fi
    else
      # The tree cannot be isolated (nothing has been touched — `--check` is a
      # dry run). Fall back to linting the worktree, and say so: unstaged changes
      # are now in scope, which is exactly what the isolation exists to prevent.
      rm -f "$_p"
      echo "pre-commit: unstaged changes can't be set aside safely (type change or" >&2
      echo "  binary diff), so linting the WORKING TREE, not the staged snapshot." >&2
    fi
  fi
  # Same git-environment strip as pre-push — see the note there. `just lint` is
  # read-only so nothing was measured failing here, but the construction is
  # identical and a lint rule that shells out to git would inherit the same
  # redirection.
  if ! (cd "$REPO_ROOT" && env -u GIT_DIR -u GIT_WORK_TREE -u GIT_IMPLICIT_WORK_TREE \
    -u GIT_INDEX_FILE -u GIT_COMMON_DIR -u GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY \
    -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES -u GIT_QUARANTINE_PATH -u GIT_PREFIX \
    -u GIT_CONFIG -u GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT -u GIT_GRAFT_FILE \
    -u GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS -u GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE -u GIT_SHALLOW_FILE \
    just lint); then
    _restore
    trap - EXIT
    echo "" >&2
    echo "❌ pre-commit: 'just lint' failed — fix the errors above before committing." >&2
    # `just lint` lints the whole tree, so untracked files are included too.
    # That's usually what you want, but it means an untracked file unrelated to
    # this commit can trip the gate — call that out so it's diagnosable rather
    # than baffling.
    if [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
      echo "   Note: untracked files are linted too; if the error is in one, it isn't part" >&2
      echo "   of this commit — check 'git status' (or 'git stash -u' them, then retry)." >&2
    fi
    echo "   (bypass in an emergency with: git commit --no-verify)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  _restore
  trap - EXIT
fi

# 2. Secret scan.
if ! command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "WARNING: gitleaks not installed — skipping local secret scan." >&2
  echo "  CI will still scan; install for fast local feedback:" >&2
  echo "    https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks#installing" >&2
  exit 0
fi

exec gitleaks git --pre-commit --staged --redact --no-banner --verbose
.github/hooks/pre-push:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pre-push hook: lifecycle gate (ADR-007).
#   1. Prevent direct pushes to main/master.
#   2. Enforce a branch type prefix — (feat|fix|chore|docs|test)/<slug> —
#      the same rule as dag_workflow.py's _BRANCH_RE. Full issue-key
#      validation (<type>/<KEY>-<n>-<slug>) runs in CI via validate-pr.yml,
#      where the linked issue can actually be checked.
# Install: .agents/scripts/install-hooks.sh

set -e

ZERO_SHA="0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"

# The push's ref lines, kept in a file: the branch rules below read them, and so
# does `gate-push check` before the fast-ci gate.
PUSH_IN="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/pre-push.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$PUSH_IN"' EXIT
cat > "$PUSH_IN"

# git feeds "<local_ref> <local_sha> <remote_ref> <remote_sha>" per ref; we only
# use local_sha + remote_ref, so the other two fields go to `_`. -r per SC2162.
PUSHING_BRANCH=0
while read -r _ local_sha remote_ref _; do
  # Branch deletions are always allowed (cleaning up misnamed branches).
  if [[ "$local_sha" == "$ZERO_SHA" ]]; then
    continue
  fi

  # Only gate branch refs — tags pass through.
  if [[ "$remote_ref" != refs/heads/* ]]; then
    continue
  fi
  branch_name="${remote_ref#refs/heads/}"
  PUSHING_BRANCH=1

  if [[ "$branch_name" == "main" || "$branch_name" == "master" ]]; then
    echo "❌ ERROR: Direct push to main/master is not allowed"
    echo ""
    echo "To contribute:"
    echo "  1. Create a new branch with the project key: git checkout -b <issue_type>/<project_abbr>-<issue_number>-<slug>"
    echo "  2. Make your changes and push: .agents/scripts/push-branch.sh"
    echo "  3. Open a PR on GitHub"
    echo ""
    echo "For more details, see .agents/project-init.md"
    exit 1
  fi

  if ! echo "$branch_name" | grep -qE '^(feat|fix|chore|docs|test)/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$'; then
    echo "❌ ERROR: branch '$branch_name' does not follow the lifecycle naming convention"
    echo ""
    echo "Enforced here: a type prefix — (feat|fix|chore|docs|test)/<slug>"
    echo "Full convention (issue key validated in CI): <issue_type>/<project_abbr>-<issue_number>-<slug>"
    echo "  Issue-linked:  feat/PI-42-add-oauth-login"
    echo "  No issue:      chore/nojira-bump-dev-dependency"
    echo ""
    echo "Use .agents/scripts/start-issue.sh or create-pr-without-issue.sh to create branches."
    exit 1
  fi
done < "$PUSH_IN"

# GIT EXPORTS ITS REPO POINTERS INTO EVERY HOOK, AND A TEST SUITE INHERITS THEM.
# `GIT_DIR` (plus `GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` in a worktree) is set by git
# for the hook process, so every `git` subprocess the recipe starts — including
# the `git init` a test runs inside its own tmpdir — is redirected back at THIS
# repository. Measured on project-init, same tree, control vs treatment:
#
#     just test                      -> 413 passed
#     GIT_DIR=<other> just test      ->   5 failed, 408 passed
#
# and on projects-orchestrator, 1508 passed -> 185 failed. The second-order
# damage is worse than the red: the tests write to the developer's INDEX, which
# is where a pile of phantom staged deletions came from. A gate that cannot pass
# when it runs is a gate people learn to push past with --no-verify, which is the
# one thing it exists to prevent.
# Fast local gate before the push leaves the machine: run `just fast-ci`
# (lint + parallel tests) — deliberately lighter than the full `just ci` so the
# push stays fast. CI re-runs the full gate (typecheck/coverage/audit + more),
# so this catches the common break (a failing test or lint error) without
# duplicating the whole suite on every push. Only fires for a real branch push
# (not tag/delete). Fail-CLOSED when `just`/the recipe are present (block the
# push, bypassable with `git push --no-verify`); fail-open when `just` or the
# `fast-ci` recipe is absent — CI stays the hard backstop. (If `just` and the
# recipe are present but a language tool is missing, the recipe itself decides:
# the day-one guards skip cleanly, a genuinely missing linter fails closed.)
if [[ "$PUSHING_BRANCH" == "1" ]]; then
  REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || (cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd))"
  if command -v just >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$REPO_ROOT/justfile" ] &&
    (cd "$REPO_ROOT" && just --show fast-ci >/dev/null 2>&1); then
    # `just fast-ci` runs against the working tree, but the push ships the
    # committed tree. If the worktree is dirty (uncommitted changes or untracked
    # files), testing it would give a false result either way — a WIP fix could
    # hide a failure in the pushed commit, or unrelated WIP could fail a clean
    # push. So skip the gate (fail-open) with a clear nudge instead of testing a
    # tree that isn't what's being pushed; CI stays the backstop.
    # A PASS ALREADY PAID FOR. git holds its push token from connect to pack
    # send, so a long fast-ci ends in HTTP 401. `gate-push` (on PATH where the
    # box provides it) runs this hook under a dry-run push, records
    # the pass, then pushes; `gate-push check` exits 0 only for that exact sha,
    # push and check set, which includes this file and the recipe declared next.
    # The branch rules above always run; only fast-ci is skipped. No gate-push on
    # PATH, or any mismatch: fast-ci runs exactly as before.
    # gate-push: cmd just --show fast-ci
    if command -v gate-push >/dev/null 2>&1 && gate-push check "$@" < "$PUSH_IN"; then
      :
    elif [ -n "$(git status --porcelain 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
      echo "pre-push: working tree is dirty — skipping the 'just fast-ci' gate" >&2
      echo "  (it would test the worktree, not the commit being pushed)." >&2
      echo "  Commit or stash your changes to run the gate before pushing." >&2
    else
      echo "pre-push: running 'just fast-ci' (lint + tests) before push…"
      # Every `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` name, plus GIT_QUARANTINE_PATH: a
      # `git -c` push exports GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS here, and an exported GIT_CONFIG
      # redirects every `git config` write (#1065).
      if ! (cd "$REPO_ROOT" && env -u GIT_DIR -u GIT_WORK_TREE -u GIT_IMPLICIT_WORK_TREE \
        -u GIT_INDEX_FILE -u GIT_COMMON_DIR -u GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY \
        -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES -u GIT_QUARANTINE_PATH -u GIT_PREFIX \
        -u GIT_CONFIG -u GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT -u GIT_GRAFT_FILE \
        -u GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS -u GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE -u GIT_SHALLOW_FILE \
        just fast-ci); then
        echo ""
        echo "❌ pre-push: 'just fast-ci' failed — fix the errors above before pushing."
        echo "   (bypass in an emergency with: git push --no-verify)"
        exit 1
      fi
    fi
  fi
fi

exit 0

.github/workflows/board-automation.yml:
name: Board automation

# Syncs issue and PR lifecycle state to GitHub Projects v2.
#
# Setup:
#   1. Create a PAT with Projects access.
#   2. Store it as PROJECT_TOKEN.
#   3. Set `github_project_number` in .agents/config.yaml to the target board
#      (the single source of truth shared with create-issue.sh / setup-github.sh).
#   4. Status field options (single-select): Backlog, To Do, In Progress,
#      In Review, Done. Optional metadata fields: Priority, Area, Size,
#      Agent ready, Confidence, Work type ("Type" is reserved by GitHub; a
#      board with a custom "Type" field from before that keeps it — #1034).
#
# Status transitions:
#   issue opened        -> Backlog   (a new ticket lands in the backlog to triage)
#   issue reopened      -> To Do     (re-enters the actionable pipeline)
#   issue closed        -> Done      (ANY close reason: merged PR, manual, dup,
#                                     not-planned, or an epic closed once its
#                                     children finish — the board must not lie)
#   PR opened (draft)   -> In Progress  (linked issue, via "Closes #N" in body)
#   PR ready_for_review -> In Review    (linked issue)
#   PR merged           -> Done         (linked issue)
#
# The `issues: closed` trigger is what keeps the board honest: without it a card
# only ever reached Done through a merged "Closes #N" PR, so every issue closed
# any other way stayed frozen in its previous column (PI board-visibility fix).

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened, edited, reopened, labeled, unlabeled, closed]
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, ready_for_review, closed]

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: read
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  board-sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    if: ${{ vars.CI_RUNS_ON == '' }}  # hosted-only: skip (not fail) when CI_RUNS_ON routes CI to a self-hosted runner
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PROJECT_TOKEN }}
      # Pin the repo so every `gh` call (e.g. `gh issue view`) resolves it
      # explicitly (PI-234).
      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
      OWNER: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
      REPO_NAME: ${{ github.event.repository.name }}

    steps:
      # Single source of truth for the board number (PI #556): read
      # `github_project_number` from .agents/config.yaml instead of a hardcoded
      # literal that drifts from what create-issue.sh / setup-github.sh provision
      # to. Account-scoped numbering means a real board is almost never #1, so a
      # hardcoded 1 here would silently split board state across two projects.
      # Needs a checkout to read the file; falls back to 1 if unset/absent.
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
      - name: Resolve PROJECT_NUMBER from config.yaml
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          num=1
          if [ -f .agents/config.yaml ]; then
            parsed=$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*github_project_number:' .agents/config.yaml \
              | head -n1 | sed 's/#.*$//' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -n1 || true)
            [ -n "$parsed" ] && num="$parsed"
          fi
          echo "PROJECT_NUMBER=$num" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "Using GitHub Project #$num (from .agents/config.yaml)"

      - name: Determine issue and status
        id: context
        env:
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
          PR_BODY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}
          PR_MERGED: ${{ github.event.pull_request.merged }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          status="skip"
          issue=""

          if [ "$EVENT" = "issues" ]; then
            issue="$ISSUE_NUMBER"
            if [ "$ACTION" = "opened" ]; then
              status="Backlog"
            elif [ "$ACTION" = "reopened" ]; then
              status="To Do"
            elif [ "$ACTION" = "closed" ]; then
              status="Done"
            else
              status="metadata"
            fi
          elif [ "$EVENT" = "pull_request" ] && [ "$ACTION" = "opened" ]; then
            issue=$(printf '%s\n' "$PR_BODY" | grep -oiP '(closes|fixes|resolves)\s+#\K[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)
            status="In Progress"
          elif [ "$EVENT" = "pull_request" ] && [ "$ACTION" = "ready_for_review" ]; then
            issue=$(printf '%s\n' "$PR_BODY" | grep -oiP '(closes|fixes|resolves)\s+#\K[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)
            status="In Review"
          elif [ "$EVENT" = "pull_request" ] && [ "$ACTION" = "closed" ] && [ "$PR_MERGED" = "true" ]; then
            issue=$(printf '%s\n' "$PR_BODY" | grep -oiP '(closes|fixes|resolves)\s+#\K[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)
            status="Done"
          fi

          echo "issue=$issue" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "status=$status" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Sync project item fields
        if: steps.context.outputs.issue != '' && steps.context.outputs.status != 'skip'
        env:
          ISSUE_NUM: ${{ steps.context.outputs.issue }}
          TARGET_STATUS: ${{ steps.context.outputs.status }}
          HAS_PROJECT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PROJECT_TOKEN != '' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          # No PROJECT_TOKEN means no board was set up for this repo (setup step
          # 2 above), and every scaffold writes a default board number, so the
          # token is the only honest "a board is configured" signal. Skip, but
          # say so where the run summary shows it rather than only in the log.
          if [ "$HAS_PROJECT_TOKEN" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice title=Board sync skipped::PROJECT_TOKEN is not set, so no board is configured for this repo."
            exit 0
          fi

          PROJECT_DATA=$(gh api graphql -f query='
            query($owner: String!, $number: Int!) {
              user(login: $owner) {
                projectV2(number: $number) {
                  id
                  fields(first: 50) {
                    nodes {
                      ... on ProjectV2SingleSelectField {
                        id
                        name
                        options { id name }
                      }
                    }
                  }
                  items(first: 100) {
                    nodes {
                      id
                      content {
                        ... on Issue { number }
                      }
                    }
                  }
                }
              }
              organization(login: $owner) {
                projectV2(number: $number) {
                  id
                  fields(first: 50) {
                    nodes {
                      ... on ProjectV2SingleSelectField {
                        id
                        name
                        options { id name }
                      }
                    }
                  }
                  items(first: 100) {
                    nodes {
                      id
                      content {
                        ... on Issue { number }
                      }
                    }
                  }
                }
              }
            }' -f owner="$OWNER" -F number="$PROJECT_NUMBER" 2>/dev/null || true)

          # A personal (user-owned) account errors on the organization(...) path
          # (and an org errors on the user(...) path); gh exits non-zero whenever
          # the response carries an `errors` array, even though valid data.user /
          # data.organization is still on stdout. Tolerate that so the jq fallback
          # below can select whichever path applies. (PI-207)
          PROJECT=$(echo "$PROJECT_DATA" | jq -c '.data.user.projectV2 // .data.organization.projectV2 // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
          PROJECT_ID=$(echo "$PROJECT" | jq -r '.id // empty')

          # A token is set, so a board is meant to be synced, and it cannot be
          # reached. This used to log "Skipping project sync" and pass, so a
          # board that had stopped syncing looked the same as one that synced.
          if [ -z "$PROJECT_ID" ]; then
            echo "::error title=Board sync failed::GitHub Project #$PROJECT_NUMBER is not reachable with PROJECT_TOKEN: the project does not exist under $OWNER, or the token lacks the project scope or has expired. Fix the token or github_project_number in .agents/config.yaml."
            exit 1
          fi

          ITEM_ID=$(echo "$PROJECT" | jq -r --argjson n "$ISSUE_NUM" '(.items.nodes // [])[] | select(.content.number == $n) | .id')

          if [ -z "$ITEM_ID" ]; then
            echo "Issue #$ISSUE_NUM not found on board; adding it first"
            ISSUE_NODE_ID=$(gh api graphql -f query='
              query($owner: String!, $repo: String!, $number: Int!) {
                repository(owner: $owner, name: $repo) {
                  issue(number: $number) { id }
                }
              }' -f owner="$OWNER" -f repo="$REPO_NAME" -F number="$ISSUE_NUM" | jq -r '.data.repository.issue.id')

            ITEM_ID=$(gh api graphql -f query='
              mutation($project: ID!, $content: ID!) {
                addProjectV2ItemById(input: { projectId: $project, contentId: $content }) {
                  item { id }
                }
              }' -f project="$PROJECT_ID" -f content="$ISSUE_NODE_ID" | jq -r '.data.addProjectV2ItemById.item.id')
          fi

          ISSUE_DATA=$(gh issue view "$ISSUE_NUM" -R "$OWNER/$REPO_NAME" --json labels,body)
          # Dual-format body parser (PI board self-population): issues reach the
          # board from three sources with two body shapes. Issue *forms* render
          # "### Heading\n\nvalue" blocks; create-issue.sh (and MCP/API-created
          # issues that mirror it) write "- Field: value" bullets. Parse BOTH so
          # Priority/Size/Agent-ready/Confidence/Area populate regardless of how
          # the issue was created (bullets take precedence, then the heading block).
          parse_body_field() {
            local heading="$1"
            local body="$2"
            local val

            # Bullet form: "- Field: value" (case-insensitive, tolerant of leading
            # indentation), trimming trailing whitespace/CR.
            val=$(printf '%s\n' "$body" \
              | sed -n "s/^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*${heading}:[[:space:]]*//Ip" \
              | head -1 | sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//')
            if [ -n "$val" ]; then
              printf '%s\n' "$val"
              return 0
            fi

            # Heading form: "### Field" followed by the value on the next non-blank line.
            printf '%s\n' "$body" | awk -v h="$heading" '
              BEGIN { in_section = 0 }
              $0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*###[[:space:]]+" h "[[:space:]]*$" { in_section = 1; next }
              in_section && /^[[:space:]]*$/ { next }
              in_section { sub(/[[:space:]]*$/, ""); print; exit }
            '
          }
          BODY=$(echo "$ISSUE_DATA" | jq -r '.body')
          PRIORITY=$(parse_body_field "Priority" "$BODY")
          SIZE=$(parse_body_field "Size" "$BODY")
          AGENT_READY=$(parse_body_field "Agent ready" "$BODY")
          CONFIDENCE=$(parse_body_field "Confidence" "$BODY")
          AREA=$(parse_body_field "Area" "$BODY")
          TYPE_LABEL=$(echo "$ISSUE_DATA" | jq -r '[.labels[].name | select(. == "feature" or . == "bug" or . == "chore" or . == "documentation" or . == "test" or . == "tech-debt" or . == "spike")][0] // empty')

          update_single_select() {
            local field_name="$1"
            local option_name="$2"
            [ -n "$option_name" ] || return 0

            local field_id
            local option_id
            field_id=$(echo "$PROJECT" | jq -r --arg f "$field_name" '(.fields.nodes // [])[] | select(.name == $f) | .id')
            if [ -z "$field_id" ]; then
              echo "Skipping missing project field: $field_name"
              return 0
            fi

            option_id=$(echo "$PROJECT" | jq -r --arg f "$field_name" --arg o "$option_name" '(.fields.nodes // [])[] | select(.name == $f) | (.options // [])[] | select(.name == $o) | .id')
            if [ -z "$option_id" ]; then
              # A warning, not a log line: the value is set on the issue but the board
              # cannot show it until the option exists (#1016).
              echo "::warning title=Board option missing::Skipping missing project option: $field_name=$option_name. Add the option to the board's '$field_name' field (setup-github.sh adds missing type options)."
              return 0
            fi

            gh api graphql -f query='
              mutation($project: ID!, $item: ID!, $field: ID!, $option: String!) {
                updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue(input: {
                  projectId: $project
                  itemId: $item
                  fieldId: $field
                  value: { singleSelectOptionId: $option }
                }) { projectV2Item { id } }
              }' -f project="$PROJECT_ID" -f item="$ITEM_ID" -f field="$field_id" -f option="$option_id"
          }

          if [ "$TARGET_STATUS" != "metadata" ]; then
            update_single_select "Status" "$TARGET_STATUS"
          fi
          update_single_select "Priority"    "$PRIORITY"
          update_single_select "Area"        "$AREA"
          update_single_select "Size"        "$SIZE"
          update_single_select "Agent ready" "$AGENT_READY"
          update_single_select "Confidence"  "$CONFIDENCE"
          # GitHub reserves "Type", so boards get "Work type" (must match
          # setup-github.sh, #1034); a board's pre-reservation "Type" still syncs.
          TYPE_FIELD="Work type"
          if ! echo "$PROJECT" | jq -e --arg f "$TYPE_FIELD" 'any((.fields.nodes // [])[]; .name == $f)' >/dev/null; then
            TYPE_FIELD="Type"
          fi
          update_single_select "$TYPE_FIELD" "$TYPE_LABEL"

          echo "Synced issue #$ISSUE_NUM to GitHub Project metadata fields"
.github/workflows/ci.yml:
name: CI

# Compute jobs read `vars.CI_RUNS_ON` (PI-666): set the repo variable to
# `self-hosted` to run CI on your own runner — the escape hatch when a private
# repo exhausts its GitHub Actions minutes. Toggle with `just ci-local-on` /
# `ci-local-off`; setup guide: .agents/docs/guides/self-hosted-ci-runner.md.
# Secret/PAT-bearing workflows deliberately stay on GitHub-hosted ephemeral runners.
# Pinned here: board-automation, issue-validation, project-init-upgrade.
# validate-pr follows CI_RUNS_ON: it is a required check and carries no PAT.


on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    # Weekly OpenSSF Scorecard security-posture run (#576). The scorecard job
    # below is schedule-gated, so it never runs — or blocks — on a PR.
    - cron: "0 4 * * 1"
    # Nightly run: the `fuzz` job in every language, plus `mutation-tests` for
    # python (PI-138/#563). Each schedule-gated job below matches on its OWN
    # cron via `github.event.schedule` — `github.event_name == 'schedule'` alone
    # fires on EVERY cron here, which silently made `fuzz` weekly for node/go/
    # rust (where this nightly entry used to be absent) and made scorecard run
    # nightly for python (PR #736 review, Copilot + Codex).
    #
    # NOTE: a cron triggers the whole workflow. Ungated jobs (lint-and-test,
    # secret-scan, semgrep, license-scan, ci-gate) run on it too — see the
    # `fuzz` job's comment for how to restrict cron runs to gated jobs only.
    - cron: "0 3 * * *"
  # Optimization: Only run CI when relevant files change
  # Uncomment and adjust paths as needed for your project

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

# Cancel a superseded run when a new commit is pushed to the SAME pull request
# (PI-589) — review cycles re-push often, and finishing an obsolete run just
# burns runner-minutes. `cancel-in-progress` is gated to pull_request events, so
# scheduled (nightly fuzz/mutation, weekly scorecard) and main-push
# runs are NEVER cancelled — they always complete. `github.event_name` is in the
# group key so those non-PR runs don't share a group (they'd otherwise serialize:
# a long nightly on main would make a main push CI queue
# behind it).
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# Job timeouts: GitHub's default is 360 min, and a hung nightly held a single
# self-hosted runner that long while deploys queued. Each bound is 1.5x the job's
# slowest completed run (success or failure, minutes, noted per job) across four
# scaffolded repos' Actions history, 2026-07-07..10-13, on hosted runners and
# 1-CPU/1-GiB self-hosted ones, rounded up to 10. Outgrow one? Raise it.
# Exceptions to that rule are marked UNMEASURED or, for mutation-tests, explained.
jobs:

  # PI-214: derive the test matrix from requires-python at runtime, so the
  # version floor can never drift from what the project itself declares (a
  # hardcoded matrix would reintroduce the PI-208 drift). This job reads
  # requires-python and emits every supported version that satisfies it;
  # lint-and-test then fans out across them. KNOWN is the only maintained
  # list — the *ceiling* set enumerated up to; bump it (or let Renovate) when
  # a new CPython is released. The floor is always taken from requires-python.
  python-matrix:
    name: Resolve Python matrix
    runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNS_ON || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    timeout-minutes: 10  # slowest 4.3
    outputs:
      versions: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.versions }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@08807647e7069bb48b6ef5acd8ec9567f424441b # v8.1.0
        with:
          version: "0.11.7"

      - name: Resolve versions satisfying requires-python
        id: resolve
        env:
          # Which cron fired (empty for push/pull_request). The resolver runs the
          # full matrix ONLY on the nightly cron — not the weekly Scorecard one.
          GITHUB_EVENT_SCHEDULE: ${{ github.event.schedule }}
        run: |
          uv run --no-project --with packaging python - <<'PY'
          import json
          import os
          import pathlib
          import tomllib

          from packaging.specifiers import InvalidSpecifier, SpecifierSet

          # Maintained ceiling set — every CPython this template is willing to
          # test. The floor comes from requires-python, else from the version
          # project-init pinned at scaffold time; never from here. Kept
          # byte-equal to SUPPORTED_PYTHON_VERSIONS in the scaffolder.
          KNOWN = ["3.11", "3.12", "3.13", "3.14"]

          def _key(v):
              return tuple(int(part) for part in v.split("."))

          spec = ""
          pyproject = pathlib.Path("pyproject.toml")
          if pyproject.is_file():
              try:
                  data = tomllib.loads(pyproject.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                  spec = data.get("project", {}).get("requires-python", "") or ""
              except (tomllib.TOMLDecodeError, OSError):
                  spec = ""

          if spec:
              try:
                  allowed = SpecifierSet(spec)
                  versions = [v for v in KNOWN if allowed.contains(v + ".0")]
              except InvalidSpecifier:
                  # Present but malformed — fall back to the full set rather
                  # than failing the job on a bad requires-python.
                  versions = list(KNOWN)
          else:
              # No requires-python yet (a fresh scaffold, #628) — honor the floor
              # project-init pinned into mise.toml and mypy.ini instead of fanning
              # out across CPythons the project never claimed to support.
              versions = [v for v in KNOWN if _key(v) >= _key("3.11")]
          if not versions:
              # requires-python excludes every KNOWN version — fall back to the
              # newest so CI still runs instead of erroring on an empty matrix.
              versions = [KNOWN[-1]]

          # Per-PR/push test only the FLOOR version for fast, cheap feedback
          # (PI-761). ONLY the nightly cron runs the full matrix — a version-
          # specific break is caught within a day. A cron triggers the whole
          # workflow, so gate on the specific schedule (github.event.schedule),
          # not event_name==schedule, or the WEEKLY Scorecard cron would fan out
          # too. "0 3 * * *" must match the nightly entry in `on.schedule` below;
          # test_ci_matrix_per_event asserts they agree.
          event = os.environ.get("GITHUB_EVENT_NAME", "")
          nightly = event == "schedule" and os.environ.get("GITHUB_EVENT_SCHEDULE", "") == "0 3 * * *"
          if not nightly and len(versions) > 1:
              versions = [min(versions, key=_key)]

          with open(os.environ["GITHUB_OUTPUT"], "a", encoding="utf-8") as out:
              out.write("versions=" + json.dumps(versions) + "\n")
          print("requires-python:", spec or '(none) -> floor 3.11 from project-init')
          print("matrix:", versions)
          PY


  lint-and-test:
    name: Lint and test
    runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNS_ON || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    timeout-minutes: 70  # slowest 40.8

    needs: python-matrix
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ${{ fromJSON(needs.python-matrix.outputs.versions) }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6


      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@08807647e7069bb48b6ef5acd8ec9567f424441b # v8.1.0
        with:
          version: "0.11.7"
          # Pin this job to the matrix version (PI-214). Not the PI-208 drift:
          # every matrix entry is >= the requires-python floor by construction
          # (see the python-matrix job), so the floor can't drift below what
          # the project declares.
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: "pyproject.toml"

      # CI invokes the same justfile recipes agents and humans use (PI-139),
      # so the command surface is defined exactly once.
      - name: Install just
        uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4
        with:
          # Pin the just binary version (#891): the action's default resolves
          # "latest" via the releases API, which intermittently returns "no
          # release matching" under GitHub API throttling and fails the job.
          just-version: "1.57.0"

      # ShellCheck ships preinstalled on ubuntu-24.04 runners; shfmt does not.
      #
      # Host-safe and OS/arch aware, because `runs-on` here is
      # `vars.CI_RUNS_ON || ubuntu-24.04` and `just ci-local-on` sets that
      # variable to `self-hosted`. Two consequences the original step got wrong:
      #
      #   1. A self-hosted runner shares $HOME with its operator. A step that
      #      writes into ~/.local/bin modifies a real machine, not a throwaway
      #      VM — so if a usable shfmt is already on PATH, leave it alone.
      #   2. The asset must match the runner. Hardcoding linux_amd64 installed a
      #      Linux x86 binary onto a macOS/ARM runner, which then failed the
      #      lint step with "cannot execute binary file" *after* overwriting the
      #      operator's working shfmt. A nightly cron repeated it unattended.
      - name: Install shfmt
        run: |
          set -eu
          if command -v shfmt >/dev/null 2>&1 && shfmt --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "shfmt $(shfmt --version) already present — leaving the host's copy alone"
            exit 0
          fi

          version="3.8.0"
          case "$(uname -s)" in
            Linux)  os=linux ;;
            Darwin) os=darwin ;;
            *) echo "unsupported OS for shfmt install: $(uname -s)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$(uname -m)" in
            x86_64|amd64)  arch=amd64 ;;
            arm64|aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
            *) echo "unsupported arch for shfmt install: $(uname -m)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          asset="shfmt_v${version}_${os}_${arch}"

          mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
          tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
          base="https://github.com/mvdan/sh/releases/download/v${version}"
          curl -sSfL "$base/$asset" -o "$tmp/$asset"
          # Verify the binary against the release's published checksums before
          # trusting it — no unverified curl|install of an executable. macOS
          # ships shasum rather than sha256sum.
          curl -sSfL "$base/sha256sums.txt" -o "$tmp/sha256sums.txt"
          if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            ( cd "$tmp" && grep " $asset\$" sha256sums.txt | sha256sum -c - )
          else
            ( cd "$tmp" && grep " $asset\$" sha256sums.txt | shasum -a 256 -c - )
          fi
          chmod +x "$tmp/$asset"
          mv "$tmp/$asset" "$HOME/.local/bin/shfmt"
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Sync dev dependencies
        run: just setup

      - name: Lint
        run: just lint

      - name: Typecheck
        run: just typecheck

      # PI-686: code-map.md's header tells agents to "read this before grepping",
      # but nothing checked it was current — the generator shipped wired only to
      # a manual `just code-map`, so the map rotted silently and agents were
      # routed to a stale index. Regenerate into a temp dir (generate-code-map.py
      # writes .agents/docs/code-map.md relative to cwd) and compare bytes;
      # never rewrite the committed file in CI. Skips cleanly before the first
      # `just code-map` run, so a fresh scaffold is not born red.
      - name: CODE_MAP is current
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          map=".agents/docs/code-map.md"
          gen=".agents/scripts/generate-code-map.py"
          # A python scaffold always ships the generator, so its absence is a
          # broken scaffold, not a not-yet-generated map — fail rather than
          # silently pass a check that can never run (PR #724 review).
          if [ ! -f "$gen" ]; then
            echo "::error file=$gen::missing — the CODE_MAP staleness check cannot run"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ ! -f "$map" ]; then
            echo "no $map yet — generate it with 'just code-map' and commit."
            exit 0
          fi
          scan="src"
          [ -d "$scan" ] || scan="."
          tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
          trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
          ( cd "$tmp" && uv run --no-project python \
              "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$gen" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$scan" >/dev/null )
          if ! cmp -s "$tmp/$map" "$map"; then
            echo "::error file=$map::code-map.md is stale — run 'just code-map' and commit"
            diff -u "$map" "$tmp/$map" | head -n 40 || true
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "$map is current."

      # Coverage gate (PI-138/PI-569): always on, not conditional — pytest-cov
      # is pulled in ephemerally via `uv run --with`, the same pattern mypy
      # (PI-558) and mutmut (PI-563) use, so there's no dev-dependency to
      # forget to add. Tune --cov-fail-under in the justfile's test-cov
      # recipe to your project's baseline; it no-ops on a fresh scaffold with
      # no src/ yet (same guard as typecheck).
      - name: Tests — parallel, coverage-gated
        run: just test-cov

      # Dependency vulnerability scan (PI-568). Complements admission_package.py,
      # which only blocks installing a package that doesn't exist or looks
      # typosquatted — this catches a real, correctly-spelled dependency
      # already in the lockfile with a known CVE/advisory.
      - name: Dependency vulnerability scan (pip-audit)
        run: just audit





      - name: Post failure summary
        if: failure() && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          PR_NUMBER="${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}"
          FAILED_STEPS=$(cat <<'SUMMARY'
          Lint or tests failed in this run. Check the details and fix before re-pushing.
          SUMMARY
          )
          gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --body "## CI failed

          **Run:** $RUN_URL

          To see what failed:
          \`\`\`bash
          gh run view --log-failed
          \`\`\`

          Fix the issues, then run \`.agents/scripts/push-branch.sh\` to re-trigger CI."


  # Optimization #2: Split heavyweight tests into separate job
  # Only run integration/smoke tests after fast lint+unit tests pass
  # Adjust this job based on your actual integration test needs.
  # Non-blocking (NOT in ci-gate's needs) — add it there once your
  # integration suite is stable enough to gate merges.
  integration-tests:
    name: Integration tests
    runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNS_ON || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    timeout-minutes: 10  # slowest 1.6
    needs: lint-and-test
    # Optional: Only run on main branch or when tests change significantly
    # if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || contains(github.event.pull_request.files[*].name, 'tests/')
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@08807647e7069bb48b6ef5acd8ec9567f424441b # v8.1.0
        with:
          version: "0.11.7"
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: "pyproject.toml"

      # uv sync installs the project's required Python (.python-version /
      # requires-python) — no version to drift (PI-208). A fresh scaffold has
      # no pyproject.toml yet — skip the sync instead of failing (same guard
      # as the justfile's `setup` recipe).
      - name: Sync dev dependencies
        run: |
          if [ ! -f pyproject.toml ]; then
            echo "No pyproject.toml yet — nothing to sync."
          elif grep -q "^\[dependency-groups\]" pyproject.toml; then
            uv sync --group dev
          else
            uv sync
          fi

      # Check if integration tests directory exists before running
      # This prevents masking real test failures with "No integration tests" message
      - name: Run integration tests
        run: |
          if [ -d tests/integration/ ]; then
            uv run pytest tests/integration/ -v --tb=short
          else
            echo "No integration tests directory found (tests/integration/)"
            echo "Create tests/integration/ when you have integration tests to run"
          fi

  # Test-quality verification via mutation testing (PI-138/#563). Mutmut is
  # slow, so it runs nightly (see the top-level `on: schedule` block), not
  # per-PR — non-blocking: not in ci-gate's `needs`, so a bad score never
  # blocks a merge. Promote it there once a real baseline is established.
  # `mutmut run` always exits 0 regardless of survivors; export-cicd-stats +
  # the score-gate step below turn the result into an actual pass/fail signal.
  # Requires a [tool.mutmut] section (source_paths = [...], scoped to
  # deterministic pure-logic modules — skip I/O-heavy code, hooks, template
  # renderers) in your own pyproject.toml; mutmut reads config from there,
  # not a standalone file like ruff.toml/mypy.ini.
  # The 120 bound is a judgement, NOT 1.5x a measured run of this command: no
  # 1-worker run exists. Small mutation sets took 5-12 min at mutmut's default
  # workers (2-4 CPUs), so 1 worker should stay well under 120. A large set (one
  # 18k-mutation repo ran 76.6 min at default workers) is projected past it:
  # measure one run with this job's command and set its own bound before adopting
  # this file. Do not set MUTMUT_MAX_CHILDREN here; the recipe owns the count.
  mutation-tests:
    name: Mutation tests (mutmut)
    runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNS_ON || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    timeout-minutes: 120  # judgement, see above
    # Nightly cron only — not the weekly Scorecard one (see `on.schedule`).
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule' && github.event.schedule == '0 3 * * *'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@08807647e7069bb48b6ef5acd8ec9567f424441b # v8.1.0
        with:
          version: "0.11.7"
      # Mutmut needs a pyproject.toml *carrying a [tool.mutmut] section* — the
      # comment above this job already says so, and source_paths is not
      # optional: without it mutmut aborts with "Could not figure out where the
      # code to mutate is."
      #
      # Testing only for the FILE is why this guard did not hold. `uv init`
      # writes a pyproject.toml on day one with no [tool.mutmut] in it, so the
      # gate opened on a project that had never configured mutation testing and
      # the nightly went red from the first commit — the failure this skip was
      # written to prevent. Test for the section, which is the thing mutmut
      # actually requires.
      - name: Check for a mutmut configuration
        id: pyproject
        run: |
          if [ -f pyproject.toml ] && grep -q '^\[tool\.mutmut\]' pyproject.toml; then
            echo "exists=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "exists=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No [tool.mutmut] section yet — skipping mutation tests."
          fi
      - if: steps.pyproject.outputs.exists == 'true'
        run: uv sync --group dev
      - name: Install just
        if: steps.pyproject.outputs.exists == 'true'
        uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4
        with:
          just-version: "1.57.0"
      # The justfile recipe, not a copy of its commands: the worker count is
      # defined once there. A bare `mutmut run` here forked os.cpu_count()
      # workers (the host's count inside a container) and hung a 1-GiB runner.
      - name: Mutation run (just test-mutation)
        if: steps.pyproject.outputs.exists == 'true'
        run: just test-mutation
      - name: Enforce mutation score gate (>= 80% killed)
        if: steps.pyproject.outputs.exists == 'true'
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import json
          import sys

          with open("mutants/mutmut-cicd-stats.json", encoding="utf-8") as f:
              stats = json.load(f)
          total = stats["total"]
          killed = stats["killed"]
          score = (killed / total * 100) if total else 100.0
          print(f"Mutation score: {score:.1f}% ({killed}/{total} killed)")
          if score < 80:
              sys.exit(f"Mutation score {score:.1f}% is below the 80% gate")
          PY


  


  # ADR-007: agent-agnostic secret-scanning backstop. The pre-commit git hook
  # gives fast local feedback but is fail-open; this job is the hard gate.
  secret-scan:
    name: Secret scan (gitleaks)
    runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNS_ON || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    timeout-minutes: 10  # slowest 2.3
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          # Full history so leaked commits are caught, not just the latest diff
          fetch-depth: 0

      # THE BINARY, NOT gitleaks/gitleaks-action (PI-933). The action refuses to
      # run on an ORGANISATION-owned repo without GITLEAKS_LICENSE — a key from
      # gitleaks.io — so every org scaffold was born with a permanently red
      # secret-scan and nothing told its owner why. That is the one job whose
      # redness is least affordable: it fails WITHOUT SCANNING, so a credential
      # in the first commit is not caught and the red mark reads as the usual
      # licence nag. A permanently red gate also trains everyone to ignore red,
      # which this file argues elsewhere in its own `fail open` comments.
      #
      # The binary has no licence gate, reads the same scaffolded .gitleaks.toml,
      # and is what `just scan` and the pre-commit hook already run — so the
      # three surfaces now agree instead of CI being the odd one out.
      #
      # IT ALSO RETIRES A SELF-HOSTED-RUNNER BUG. The action downloaded to a
      # FIXED $TMPDIR/gitleaks.tmp, aborted if that path existed, and never
      # cleaned up. Hosted runners hid it by discarding the machine; on a
      # self-hosted runner the first GREEN run poisoned every run after it and
      # the repo silently stopped being scanned while the job merely looked
      # flaky (measured 2026-08-01: green at 20:43:55, red 88 s later, red for
      # the following two days). Extracting into $RUNNER_TEMP, which the runner
      # empties per job on both kinds, makes the path fresh by construction.
      #
      # OS AND ARCH ARE READ FROM THE RUNNER, NOT ASSUMED. `runs-on` is
      # overridable via vars.CI_RUNS_ON, and the runner that found the bug above
      # was self-hosted macOS — a hardcoded linux_x64 asset would 404 there and
      # the gate would fail for a reason unrelated to secrets.
      #
      # THE DOWNLOAD IS VERIFIED. Replacing a SHA-pinned action with a curl is a
      # supply-chain downgrade unless the bytes are checked, so the release's own
      # checksums file is fetched and the tarball verified against it before
      # anything is executed. That detects a corrupted or truncated download and
      # a CDN-level substitution; it cannot detect a compromised release, which
      # is what the version pin below is for.
      - name: Install gitleaks
        env:
          # THE MARKER IS WHAT MAKES THE PIN MAINTAINED, not decoration. Renovate
          # sees `uses:` digests and lockfiles; a version literal in a shell step
          # is invisible to every built-in manager, so without this line the
          # scanner would freeze at 8.30.1 with no signal while everything else
          # stayed current — a security tool rotting quietly is worse than an
          # unpinned one. renovate.json's customManagers entry reads it.
          # renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=gitleaks/gitleaks
          GITLEAKS_VERSION: 8.30.1
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$RUNNER_OS" in
            Linux) os=linux ;;
            macOS) os=darwin ;;
            *) echo "::error::unsupported RUNNER_OS=$RUNNER_OS"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$RUNNER_ARCH" in
            X64) arch=x64 ;;
            ARM64) arch=arm64 ;;
            *) echo "::error::unsupported RUNNER_ARCH=$RUNNER_ARCH"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          base="https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v${GITLEAKS_VERSION}"
          asset="gitleaks_${GITLEAKS_VERSION}_${os}_${arch}.tar.gz"
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP"
          curl -sSfL --retry 3 -o "$asset" "${base}/${asset}"
          curl -sSfL --retry 3 -o checksums.txt "${base}/gitleaks_${GITLEAKS_VERSION}_checksums.txt"
          # EXACT FIELD MATCH, NOT A grep PATTERN (PR #940 review). `grep
          # " ${asset}$"` reads as an exact selection and is not one: the asset
          # name is full of dots and grep treats them as "any character", so the
          # line whose checksum gets verified is chosen by a regex that also
          # matches names nobody intended. No sibling asset in this manifest
          # differs from another only at a dot, so it cannot mis-select today —
          # which is exactly why it would go unnoticed when a future asset name
          # makes it possible. awk compares field 2 for equality and prints the
          # line verbatim, so the format shasum expects is preserved.
          #
          # AND IT MUST FAIL WHEN NOTHING MATCHES. `exit !found` is why: an empty
          # expected.sha256 handed to a verifier is a check that reports success
          # on no input, which is the shape of a gate that guards nothing.
          awk -v a="$asset" '$2 == a { print; found = 1 } END { exit !found }' \
            checksums.txt > expected.sha256
          if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            sha256sum -c expected.sha256
          else
            shasum -a 256 -c expected.sha256
          fi
          tar -xzf "$asset" gitleaks
          chmod 0755 gitleaks
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          ./gitleaks version

      - name: Scan full history
        # --redact so a finding never prints the secret into a public log.
        run: gitleaks git --redact --no-banner --verbose .

  # Semgrep: semantic/AST security backstop. gitleaks (above) is string-
  # pattern secret scanning; semgrep catches unsafe subprocess calls, SQL
  # injection, and other OWASP Top 10 shapes gitleaks can't see. Explicit
  # rulesets (not --config=auto) for reproducibility. Not in ci-gate's
  # needs — a finding never blocks a merge while the false-positive rate is
  # calibrated, but --error still fails this job's own step so findings are
  # visible. Promote to ci-gate's needs once calibrated.
  semgrep:
    name: Semgrep (semantic security scan)
    runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNS_ON || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    timeout-minutes: 20  # slowest 11.3
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          # Full history: --baseline-commit (PR-only, below) needs the base
          # commit reachable, not just the latest diff.
          fetch-depth: 0

      # uvx (not bare `pip`): a self-hosted runner has no writable system
      # site-packages, so `pip install semgrep` fails there (externally-managed
      # env). uvx runs it from an ephemeral, pinned env on hosted and
      # self-hosted alike (CI_RUNS_ON switch, PI-666/PI-673).
      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@08807647e7069bb48b6ef5acd8ec9567f424441b # v8.1.0
        with:
          version: "0.11.7"

      - name: Run Semgrep
        env:
          SEMGREP_ENABLE_VERSION_CHECK: "0"
        run: |
          SEMGREP="uvx semgrep@1.168.0"
          RULESETS="--config p/secrets --config p/owasp-top-ten --config p/python"
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
            # Scan only the diff against the PR's base commit.
            $SEMGREP scan --error --metrics=off $RULESETS \
              --baseline-commit "${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          else
            $SEMGREP scan --error --metrics=off $RULESETS
          fi

  # Dependency license compliance (#579): flag copyleft (GPL/AGPL) dependencies
  # pulled in transitively — a permissive-licensed project (MIT/Apache-2.0)
  # usually must not ship them. Free/OSS tooling per language, no paid service,
  # runs entirely in CI. Non-blocking initially (NOT in ci-gate's needs) while
  # the deny-list is calibrated — the same rollout semgrep/scorecard used;
  # promote it into ci-gate once your license policy is settled. The deny-list
  # lives in the justfile's `license` recipe (or deny.toml for Rust).
  license-scan:
    name: Dependency license scan
    runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNS_ON || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    timeout-minutes: 20  # slowest 6.9
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6

      - name: Install just
        uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4
        with:
          # Pin the just binary version (#891): the action's default resolves
          # "latest" via the releases API, which intermittently returns "no
          # release matching" under GitHub API throttling and fails the job.
          just-version: "1.57.0"

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@08807647e7069bb48b6ef5acd8ec9567f424441b # v8.1.0
        with:
          version: "0.11.7"

      - name: License scan (pip-licenses)
        run: just license

  # Property-based testing / fuzzing (#580, #727). `just fuzz` exists in every
  # language, so it runs in CI in every language — previously only Go had a job,
  # and the other three shipped a recipe nothing ever invoked: dead surface that
  # reads as covered.
  #
  # WHY NIGHTLY, NOT PER-PR (#727). Fuzzing is a pattern for surfacing edge
  # cases, not a uniform gate like ruff or coverage. Per-PR it would tax every
  # push for near-zero value on a fresh scaffold. Nightly is also where it earns
  # its keep: Hypothesis, proptest and fast-check draw FRESH random seeds each
  # run, so a nightly job explores inputs a per-PR run would only repeat. (Go's
  # `go test -run=Fuzz` is a deterministic seed-corpus replay, so it gains
  # nothing from repetition — but uniformity across the four languages is worth
  # more than one job placed differently.) This is the same rollout mutation
  # testing already uses: schedule-gated, non-blocking, promote when you have a
  # baseline worth gating on.
  #
  # Non-blocking: NOT in ci-gate's `needs`. To gate on it, add a `-fuzztime`
  # active-fuzzing step and promote it there deliberately.
  #
  # Only one language renders per scaffold, so exactly one `fuzz` job exists.
  #
  # COST, STATED HONESTLY (PR #736 review). A cron entry triggers the WHOLE
  # workflow, not just the jobs gated on it. The nightly cron therefore also runs
  # every ungated job — `lint-and-test`, `secret-scan`, `semgrep`, `license-scan`
  # — plus `ci-gate`. Python scaffolds have behaved this way since the nightly
  # mutmut cron landed (#563); #727 extends the same nightly run to node/go/rust.
  # To make cron runs execute ONLY the schedule-gated jobs, add
  # `if: github.event_name != 'schedule'` to each ungated job AND to `ci-gate`
  # — `ci-gate` is `if: always()` and treats a skipped `needs` job as a failure,
  # so gating the others without gating it turns every nightly run red.
  #
  # The `if:` matches the NIGHTLY cron specifically. `github.event_name ==
  # 'schedule'` alone fires on every cron in `on.schedule`, which would make
  # this job weekly-and-nightly and (worse) couple unrelated jobs' cadences.
  fuzz:
    name: Fuzz / property tests
    runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNS_ON || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    timeout-minutes: 20  # slowest 11.0
    # Nightly cron only — not the weekly Scorecard one (see `on.schedule`).
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule' && github.event.schedule == '0 3 * * *'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6

      - name: Install just
        uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4
        with:
          # Pin the just binary version (#891): the action's default resolves
          # "latest" via the releases API, which intermittently returns "no
          # release matching" under GitHub API throttling and fails the job.
          just-version: "1.57.0"

      # A fresh scaffold has nothing to fuzz. Skip rather than fail: a nightly
      # run that is red from day one is a notification people learn to ignore.
      # Only one language renders per scaffold, so testing all four names needs
      # no per-language variable.
      #
      # A MANIFEST IS NOT THE SAME THING AS SOMETHING TO FUZZ, and testing only
      # for the manifest is why this guard did not hold. `uv init` (or
      # `npm init`, `go mod init`, `cargo init`) writes one on day one — long
      # before the first test exists — which opens the gate on an empty project.
      # pytest then exits 5, "no tests collected", and the nightly is red from
      # the first commit: exactly the outcome the skip exists to prevent.
      # Observed on a scaffold whose pyproject.toml came from `uv init` and
      # which had no tests/ directory at all.
      #
      # The prunes matter: .venv and node_modules are full of third-party test
      # files, and finding one of those would re-open the gate on a project
      # that still has none of its own.
      - name: Check for something to fuzz
        id: manifest
        run: |
          if [ ! -f pyproject.toml ] && [ ! -f package.json ] && [ ! -f go.mod ] && [ ! -f Cargo.toml ]; then
            echo "exists=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No project manifest yet — nothing to fuzz."
          # NO BARE DIRECTORY CHECK. `[ -d tests ]` counted an EMPTY tests/ as
          # a test, so the gate opened and `just fuzz` then died the way this
          # step exists to prevent: pytest exits 5 on "no tests collected", and
          # a placeholder directory is the most common shape of a young repo.
          # The patterns below already search tests/ recursively, so nothing is
          # lost by requiring an actual file.
          elif find . \
                 \( -name .git -o -name .venv -o -name node_modules \
                    -o -name target -o -name vendor \) -prune -o \
                 \( -name 'test_*.py' -o -name '*_test.py' -o -name '*_test.go' \
                    -o -name '*.test.ts' -o -name '*.test.tsx' -o -name '*.test.js' \
                    -o -name '*.spec.ts' -o -name '*.spec.tsx' -o -name '*.spec.js' \
                    -o -name '*_spec.ts' -o -name '*_spec.js' \
                    -o -path '*/tests/*.rs' \) \
                 -print -quit | grep -q .; then
            echo "exists=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # RUST KEEPS ITS TESTS INSIDE THE SOURCE FILE. `#[cfg(test)]` modules and
          # `proptest!` blocks live in src/*.rs, which matches none of the filename
          # patterns above — so a Rust crate testing the conventional way scored
          # exists=false and SILENTLY LOST nightly fuzz coverage the older
          # manifest-based gate had given it. -F because the literal contains
          # regex metacharacters.
          # `#[test]` ALONE IS A TEST. Cargo runs a bare `#[test]` fn with no
          # surrounding `#[cfg(test)]` module, so requiring the cfg spelling
          # suppressed the job for a validly tested crate. The search also covers
          # WORKSPACES via `*/src`, because a Cargo workspace keeps its crates in
          # subdirectories and grepping only the root src/ found nothing in any of
          # them. Deliberately NOT `.`: that would sweep target/ and any vendored
          # crate, so a dependency's tests would open the gate for a crate with
          # none of its own. An unmatched `*/src` glob stays literal and -s
          # swallows the resulting error.
          elif [ -f Cargo.toml ] && find . \
                 \( -name target -o -name vendor -o -name .git \) -prune -o \
                 -path '*/src/*' -name '*.rs' \
                 -exec grep -lsF -e '#[test]' -e '#[cfg(test)]' -e 'proptest!' {} + \
               2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
            echo "exists=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "exists=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "Manifest present but no tests yet — nothing to fuzz."
          fi

      - name: Install uv
        if: steps.manifest.outputs.exists == 'true'
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@08807647e7069bb48b6ef5acd8ec9567f424441b # v8.1.0
        with:
          version: "0.11.7"
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: "pyproject.toml"

      - name: Run property/fuzz tests
        if: steps.manifest.outputs.exists == 'true'
        run: just fuzz

  # OpenSSF Scorecard (#576): standardized security-posture scoring (branch
  # protection, dependency pinning, SAST presence, token permissions, ...).
  # Schedule-only + non-blocking (NOT in ci-gate's needs) — a score is
  # informational, mirroring how semgrep/mutmut were introduced. It surfaces the
  # signal that most of the gates already shipped here would score well against.
  #
  # publish_results is FALSE by default: turning a scaffolded project's score
  # into a PUBLIC entry on the scorecard.dev dashboard is an explicit opt-in the
  # project owner must choose, never something the scaffolder silently enables.
  # To opt in, flip publish_results to true below (id-token: write is already
  # granted so the OIDC upload to the public dashboard works).
  scorecard:
    name: OpenSSF Scorecard
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04  # pinned: OSSF scorecard-action requires GitHub-hosted runners
    timeout-minutes: 10  # slowest 1.0
    # Weekly cron only — not the nightly one (see `on.schedule`). Skipped (not
    # failed) when CI_RUNS_ON routes CI to a self-hosted runner: it can never start there.
    if: vars.CI_RUNS_ON == '' && github.event_name == 'schedule' && github.event.schedule == '0 4 * * 1'
    permissions:
      security-events: write   # upload the SARIF result to code scanning
      id-token: write          # only needed if publish_results is turned on
      contents: read
      actions: read            # Scorecard reads workflow/branch-protection state
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Full version pin: ossf/scorecard-action publishes no floating `v2`
      # major tag (only exact vX.Y.Z tags), so `@v2` fails to resolve.
      - name: Run Scorecard analysis
        uses: ossf/scorecard-action@4eaacf0543bb3f2c246792bd56e8cdeffafb205a # v2.4.3
        with:
          results_file: results.sarif
          results_format: sarif
          # PUBLIC-dashboard publishing stays OFF by default (#576) — flip to
          # true only to deliberately publish this repo's score to scorecard.dev.
          publish_results: false

      # In-repo visibility: the score shows up under the Security → Code scanning
      # tab without ever leaving the repository.
      - name: Upload SARIF to code scanning
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@411c4c9a36b3fca4d674f06b6396b2c6d23522c6 # v3
        with:
          sarif_file: results.sarif

  # All-green gate (PI #555): the SINGLE required status check for branch
  # protection. Branch protection requires only "CI gate", so the required
  # context is robust to matrix changes — adding/removing a Python version
  # never renames the required check, and there is no un-expanded matrix name
  # (e.g. "Lint and test (3.11)") for GitHub to fail to match against, which is
  # what left main permanently `blocked` before. `if: always()` so the gate runs
  # even when an upstream job fails, then fails itself unless every dependency
  # succeeded.
  # The governance job (when the overlay is on) is in the gate's needs: its
  # comment calls it "the enforcement boundary", which is only true if a
  # failing gate actually blocks the merge.
  ci-gate:
    name: CI gate
    runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNS_ON || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}  # must follow the variable: it is the REQUIRED check — pinned, it can't start during a billing lockout and blocks the merge
    timeout-minutes: 10  # slowest 1.8
    needs: [lint-and-test, secret-scan]
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Require all upstream jobs to succeed
        env:
          RESULTS: ${{ join(needs.*.result, ' ') }}
        run: |
          echo "Upstream job results: $RESULTS"
          for result in $RESULTS; do
            if [ "$result" != "success" ]; then
              echo "::error::A required job did not succeed (got: $result)."
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "All required jobs passed."


# Optimization #3: Conditional job execution
# Example configurations for different scenarios (see full details in CLAUDE.md):
#
# Path filters: Only run CI when relevant files change
# Skip tests for docs-only changes: Use GitHub Actions conditional if statements
# Skip integration tests for PRs from forks: Use event filters
# See GitHub Actions documentation for complete conditionals syntax
.github/workflows/issue-validation.yml:
name: Validate issue metadata

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened, edited, reopened, labeled, unlabeled]

permissions:
  issues: write

jobs:
  validate-issue:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    if: ${{ vars.CI_RUNS_ON == '' }}  # hosted-only: skip (not fail) when CI_RUNS_ON routes CI to a self-hosted runner
    steps:
      - name: Validate required planning metadata
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # This job has no actions/checkout — it only needs the issue payload,
          # not the tree. But `gh` falls back to reading the git remote to work
          # out which repo it is talking to, and with no checkout there is no
          # git repo, so every `gh issue edit` / `gh label create` below died
          # with "failed to run git: fatal: not a git repository" and the job
          # exited 1. It had NEVER passed in any scaffolded repo — 100% failure
          # across every run in three of them, which is why nobody read it.
          # GH_REPO tells gh the repo directly and skips the git lookup, which
          # is cheaper than adding a checkout just to satisfy a remote lookup.
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
          ISSUE_BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
          LABELS_JSON: ${{ toJson(github.event.issue.labels) }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          missing=()

          has_body_value() {
            local name="$1"
            local bullet_pattern="^- ${name}: (unset|[[:space:]]*)$"
            if ! printf '%s\n' "$ISSUE_BODY" | grep -qiE "$name"; then
              missing+=("$name")
              return
            fi
            if printf '%s\n' "$ISSUE_BODY" | grep -qiE "$bullet_pattern"; then
              missing+=("$name")
            fi
          }

          # Map a body "Type" value (either the create-issue.sh type keyword —
          # feat/fix/chore/docs/test — or the label name itself) to the canonical
          # type label. spike and debt/tech-debt are LABEL-only types: a spike
          # does not branch and tech-debt branches as fix/ or chore/, so the
          # keyword alphabet (create-issue.sh, start-issue.sh, branch names) does
          # not carry them.
          map_type_label() {
            case "$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" in
            feat | feature) echo "feature" ;;
            fix | bug) echo "bug" ;;
            chore) echo "chore" ;;
            docs | documentation) echo "documentation" ;;
            test) echo "test" ;;
            spike) echo "spike" ;;
            debt | tech-debt) echo "tech-debt" ;;
            *) echo "" ;;
            esac
          }

          # Derive the type from the body, tolerating both the "- Type: value"
          # bullet (create-issue.sh / MCP-API issues) and the "### Type" heading
          # block (issue forms).
          parse_type_from_body() {
            local body="$1" val
            val=$(printf '%s\n' "$body" | sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*Type:[[:space:]]*//Ip' | head -1 | sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//')
            if [ -z "$val" ]; then
              val=$(printf '%s\n' "$body" | awk '
                BEGIN { in_s = 0 }
                /^[[:space:]]*###[[:space:]]+Type[[:space:]]*$/ { in_s = 1; next }
                in_s && /^[[:space:]]*$/ { next }
                in_s { sub(/[[:space:]]*$/, ""); print; exit }
              ')
            fi
            printf '%s\n' "$val"
          }

          # Issues created via the GitHub MCP/API can't create labels or set them,
          # so they land with no valid type label. Derive the type from the body's
          # "- Type:" (or "### Type"), create the mapped label if missing, and apply
          # it (this job already has issues: write). Only fall back to flagging
          # "type label" as missing when the body carries no recognizable type.
          has_type_label() {
            if printf '%s\n' "$LABELS_JSON" | jq -e 'any(.[].name; . == "feature" or . == "bug" or . == "chore" or . == "documentation" or . == "test" or . == "tech-debt" or . == "spike")' >/dev/null; then
              return
            fi
            local body_type label
            body_type=$(parse_type_from_body "$ISSUE_BODY")
            label=$(map_type_label "$body_type")
            if [ -z "$label" ]; then
              missing+=("type label")
              return
            fi
            gh label create "$label" --color "0075ca" --description "Issue type" 2>/dev/null || true
            if gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --add-label "$label"; then
              echo "Applied type label '$label' (derived from body Type '$body_type')."
            else
              missing+=("type label")
            fi
          }

          # Dual-format body field reader (bullet "- Field: value" wins, else the
          # "### Field" heading block) — the same parser board-automation.yml uses.
          parse_body_field() {
            local heading="$1" body="$2" val
            val=$(printf '%s\n' "$body" \
              | sed -n "s/^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*${heading}:[[:space:]]*//Ip" \
              | head -1 | sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//')
            if [ -n "$val" ]; then
              printf '%s\n' "$val"
              return 0
            fi
            printf '%s\n' "$body" | awk -v h="$heading" '
              BEGIN { in_section = 0 }
              $0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*###[[:space:]]+" h "[[:space:]]*$" { in_section = 1; next }
              in_section && /^[[:space:]]*$/ { next }
              in_section { sub(/[[:space:]]*$/, ""); print; exit }
            '
          }

          # Turn the body's free-text Area value into facetable area:<slug>
          # label(s) so issues are filterable by subsystem in the UI, mirroring the
