#!/usr/bin/env sh
# doc-check.sh -- docs front matter and generated-file headers, judged by the standard's doc-shape.sh.
#
#   sh gates/doc-check.sh             report findings (the controls are born warn: exit 0)
#   sh gates/doc-check.sh --strict    any finding is red, exit 1
#
# THE JUDGES are vendor/naming/doc-shape.sh (docs/**/*.md carry kind, owner and status; a generated-by header
# equals its contracts/fresh-checks.tsv row) and vendor/naming/doc-fresh-verify.sh (is each generated file
# current). Both ship in the vendored package, so CI needs no checkout of the standard. DOC_ROOT=<dir>
# judges <dir> while the judges stay the ones beside this script. No vendored package: UNCHECKED, exit 3.
set -eu
PKG_HOME=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "${DOC_ROOT:-$PKG_HOME}" && pwd)
V="$PKG_HOME/vendor/naming"
for f in doc-shape.sh doc-fresh-verify.sh; do
  [ -f "$V/$f" ] || { printf 'doc-check: UNCHECKED, vendor/naming/%s is missing (re-vendor: sh <standard checkout>/bin/standard-vendor.sh .)\n' "$f" >&2; exit 3; }
done
rc=0
sh "$V/doc-shape.sh" --root "$ROOT" --registry "$V/registry" "$@" || rc=1
if [ -f "$ROOT/contracts/fresh-checks.tsv" ]; then
  sh "$V/doc-fresh-verify.sh" --root "$ROOT" || rc=1
fi
exit "$rc"
gates/naming-check.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env sh
# naming-check.sh -- the naming standard over this repo, as a ratchet.
#
#   sh gates/naming-check.sh          judge the tree; exit 0 clean, 1 red, 3 UNCHECKED
#   sh gates/naming-check.sh --seed   write gates/naming.baseline from today's findings
#                                     (adoption only: refuses a baseline that already has rows)
#
# THE JUDGE is the standard's lint-name.sh. This repo carries it vendored in vendor/naming/
# (refresh: `sh <standard checkout>/bin/standard-vendor.sh .`), so CI needs no checkout. With no
# vendored package the gate falls back to a checkout of the standard's source named by
# $NAMING_SOURCE (a directory holding bin/lint-name.sh and standards/naming/). With neither it
# says UNCHECKED and exits 3: never a silent pass.
#
# THE RATCHET. gates/naming.baseline holds one finding per line (`rule TAB subject`):
#   NEW    a finding not in the baseline                   -> red: fix the name
#   STALE  a baselined finding that no longer occurs       -> red: delete its line
# The baseline only shrinks. A new finding is fixed, never added by hand to the file.
#
# EXEMPTIONS. A name the standard must not judge is a row in naming-exemptions.tsv at the repo
# root (same columns as the vendored registry/exemptions.tsv), appended to a temporary copy of
# the registry. Rules that judge the registry itself are dropped: the standard's owner judges those.
#
# WHAT IS JUDGED is the working tree as git would commit it (tracked plus untracked-not-ignored),
# read through a throwaway index, so an uncommitted scaffold is judged and nothing is staged.
# Outside a git repository a throwaway git dir lists the same tree.
#
# ANOTHER ROOT. NAMING_ROOT=<dir> judges <dir>, with <dir>'s naming-exemptions.tsv and baseline,
# while the judge stays the one beside this script. Unset, the root is this script's own repo.
set -eu
PKG_HOME=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
[ -z "${NAMING_ROOT:-}" ] || [ -d "$NAMING_ROOT" ] || { printf 'naming-check: NAMING_ROOT is not a directory: %s\n' "$NAMING_ROOT" >&2; exit 2; }
ROOT=$(cd "${NAMING_ROOT:-$PKG_HOME}" && pwd)
VENDOR="$PKG_HOME/vendor/naming"
cd "$ROOT"
BASELINE="${NAMING_BASELINE:-gates/naming.baseline}"
EXEMPTIONS="naming-exemptions.tsv"
MODE=check
case "${1:-}" in
  "") ;;
  --seed) MODE=seed ;;
  *) printf 'usage: sh gates/naming-check.sh [--seed]\n' >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

unchecked() { printf 'naming-check: UNCHECKED, %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 3; }

T=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/naming-check.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT INT TERM HUP

if [ -f "$VENDOR/lint-name.sh" ] && [ -d "$VENDOR/registry" ]; then
  LINT="$VENDOR/lint-name.sh"
  REGSRC="$VENDOR/registry"
  if [ -f "$VENDOR/standard-vendor.sh" ] && [ -f "$VENDOR/MANIFEST.tsv" ]; then
    vrc=0
    sh "$VENDOR/standard-vendor.sh" --check --offline "$PKG_HOME" > "$T/vendor.out" 2>&1 || vrc=$?
    if [ "$vrc" -ne 0 ]; then
      cat "$T/vendor.out" >&2
      [ "$vrc" -eq 3 ] && unchecked "the vendored package cannot be verified against its manifest"
      printf 'naming-check: RED, vendor/naming/ differs from its MANIFEST.tsv. Restore it or re-vendor: sh <standard checkout>/bin/standard-vendor.sh .\n' >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  fi
else
  SRC="${NAMING_SOURCE:-}"
  [ -n "$SRC" ] && [ -f "$SRC/bin/lint-name.sh" ] && [ -d "$SRC/standards/naming" ] ||
    unchecked "no vendor/naming/ in this repo and no standard checkout (vendor it: sh <standard checkout>/bin/standard-vendor.sh $PKG_HOME, or set NAMING_SOURCE)"
  LINT="$SRC/bin/lint-name.sh"
  REGSRC="$SRC/standards/naming"
fi

cp -R "$REGSRC" "$T/registry"
if [ -f "$EXEMPTIONS" ]; then
  grep -v -e '^#' -e '^id	' -e '^[[:space:]]*$' "$EXEMPTIONS" >> "$T/registry/exemptions.tsv" || :
fi

# lint-name judges the files git lists. Use this repo's git when it has one; a scaffold that is not
# a repository yet gets a throwaway git dir over the same work tree, so it is judged, not skipped.
if ! git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  git init -q --bare "$T/gitdir" > /dev/null 2>&1 || unchecked "git is not available to list the tree"
  GIT_DIR="$T/gitdir"; GIT_WORK_TREE="$ROOT"; export GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE
fi
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$T/index"; export GIT_INDEX_FILE
git add -A -- . > /dev/null 2>&1 || unchecked "could not read the working tree through git"
rc=0
# Hermetic: a clean environment and an empty HOME, so the judge reads no term overlay or pack terms from the box
# (CI has neither) and a baseline seeded here is the one CI judges against.
mkdir "$T/home"
set -- PATH="$PATH" HOME="$T/home" TMPDIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" GIT_INDEX_FILE="$GIT_INDEX_FILE"
[ -z "${GIT_DIR:-}" ] || set -- "$@" GIT_DIR="$GIT_DIR" GIT_WORK_TREE="$GIT_WORK_TREE"
env -i "$@" sh "$LINT" --root "$ROOT" --registry "$T/registry" --format findings > "$T/out" 2> "$T/err" || rc=$?
unset GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE
if [ "$rc" -gt 1 ]; then
  cat "$T/err" >&2
  unchecked "lint-name exited $rc"
fi

# One `rule TAB subject` per finding; the A/V column is the rule's mode, which may change without the finding changing.
awk -F'\t' 'NF >= 3 && $2 !~ /^name\.(registry-|exemption-|alias|control-|surface-)/ { print $2 "\t" $3 }' "$T/out" | LC_ALL=C sort -u > "$T/now"

if [ "$MODE" = seed ]; then
  if [ -f "$BASELINE" ] && grep -q -v -e '^#' -e '^[[:space:]]*$' "$BASELINE"; then
    printf 'naming-check: %s already has rows; --seed is for adoption and will not overwrite them\n' "$BASELINE" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$BASELINE")"
  {
    printf '# naming baseline: findings the tree carried when the naming gate was adopted. rule TAB subject.\n'
    printf '# This file only SHRINKS: a line whose finding no longer occurs turns the gate red until it is\n'
    printf '# deleted; a new finding is fixed, never added here.\n'
    cat "$T/now"
  } > "$BASELINE"
  printf 'naming-check: seeded %s with %s finding(s)\n' "$BASELINE" "$(wc -l < "$T/now" | tr -d ' ')" >&2
  exit 0
fi

[ -f "$BASELINE" ] || {
  printf 'naming-check: RED, no baseline at %s. An empty file is a valid baseline; a missing one is not (seed: sh gates/naming-check.sh --seed).\n' "$BASELINE" >&2
  exit 1
}
grep -v -e '^#' -e '^[[:space:]]*$' "$BASELINE" | LC_ALL=C sort -u > "$T/base" || :

LC_ALL=C comm -23 "$T/now" "$T/base" > "$T/new"
LC_ALL=C comm -13 "$T/now" "$T/base" > "$T/stale"
nn=$(wc -l < "$T/new" | tr -d ' ')
ns=$(wc -l < "$T/stale" | tr -d ' ')
nb=$(wc -l < "$T/base" | tr -d ' ')
nnow=$(wc -l < "$T/now" | tr -d ' ')

[ "$nn" -eq 0 ] || { printf 'NEW (fix the name; do not baseline it):\n'; sed 's/^/  /' "$T/new"; }
[ "$ns" -eq 0 ] || { printf 'STALE (fixed; delete these lines from %s):\n' "$BASELINE"; sed 's/^/  /' "$T/stale"; }
printf 'naming-check: %s finding(s) now, %s baselined, %s new, %s stale\n' "$nnow" "$nb" "$nn" "$ns"
[ "$nn" -eq 0 ] && [ "$ns" -eq 0 ]
gates/naming.baseline:
# naming baseline: findings the tree carried when the naming gate was adopted. rule TAB subject.
# This file only SHRINKS: a line whose finding no longer occurs turns the gate red until it is
# deleted; a new finding is fixed, never added here. Seed it once with: sh gates/naming-check.sh --seed
justfile:
# justfile — the canonical command interface (scaffolded by project-init).
# `just --list` shows every recipe. Recipes are thin wrappers — logic lives
# in the tools and their configs, never in this file.

# install/sync dev dependencies (PEP 735 dependency-group; add tools with `uv add --dev`).
# A fresh scaffold has no pyproject.toml (or one without [dependency-groups])
# yet — `uv sync --group dev` hard-fails on both, which would break CI's first
# step before the day-one guards in typecheck/test-cov can even run.
[doc("install/sync dev dependencies (PEP 735 dependency-group; add tools with `uv add --dev`).")]
setup:
    sh -c 'if [ ! -f pyproject.toml ]; then echo "No pyproject.toml yet — nothing to sync."; elif grep -q "^\[dependency-groups\]" pyproject.toml; then uv sync --group dev; else uv sync; fi'

# lint project code (docstring + complexity gates per ruff.toml).
# `ruff format --check` verifies formatting without writing — `just format`
# writes. Without this, an unformatted file merged green (#726).
[doc("lint project code (docstring + complexity gates per ruff.toml).")]
lint:
    uv run ruff check .
    uv run ruff format --check .
    sh -c 'if command -v shellcheck >/dev/null 2>&1; then find .agents -name "*.sh" -exec shellcheck -S error -x {} +; else echo "shellcheck not installed — skipping shell lint (CI still runs it). Install: https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck#installing or run \`mise install\`."; fi'
    sh -c 'if command -v shfmt >/dev/null 2>&1; then find .agents -name "*.sh" -exec shfmt -d -i 2 {} +; else echo "shfmt not installed — skipping shfmt check (CI still runs it). Install: https://github.com/mvdan/sh#shfmt or run \`mise install\`."; fi'
    bash .agents/scripts/lint-context-budget.sh
    just naming
    just docs-check
    uv run python .agents/scripts/check-test-contract.py exit-codes
    uv run --with pytest python .agents/scripts/check-test-contract.py discovery

# static type check (strict mode per mypy.ini; add mypy with `uv add --dev mypy`)
# no-op on a fresh scaffold with no src/ yet — mypy errors on a missing path.
# --install-types fetches missing dependency stubs (types-PyYAML etc.) so
# untyped deps don't fail the strict gate with import-untyped (#592); it
# shells out to pip, which uv-managed environments omit — hence --with pip.
[doc("static type check (strict mode per mypy.ini; add mypy with `uv add --dev mypy`)")]
typecheck:
    if [ -d src ]; then uv run --with "mypy>=1.10" --with pip mypy --install-types --non-interactive src/; else echo "No src/ directory yet — nothing to type-check."; fi

# auto-format project code
format:
    uv run ruff format .

# run the test suite (xdist pulled in on demand so -n works without declaring it).
# The cross-repo test contract (PI-1044): it ends with `<project>: N passed, M failed`,
# printed by the root conftest.py, and exits with pytest's own code.
[doc("run the test suite; ends with `<project>: N passed, M failed` (the test contract)")]
test:
    sh -c 'if find tests -type f \( -name "test_*.py" -o -name "*_test.py" \) 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then uv run --with pytest-xdist pytest -n auto --tb=short -q; else echo "No test files yet — nothing to test."; echo "projects-orchestrator: 0 passed, 0 failed"; fi'

# fail-fast quiet run for the edit-test loop (token-efficiency; PI-641) —
# stops at the first failure so agents ingest one traceback, not the suite's
[doc("fail-fast quiet run for the edit-test loop (token-efficiency; PI-641)")]
test-quick:
    sh -c 'if find tests -type f \( -name "test_*.py" -o -name "*_test.py" \) 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then uv run --with pytest pytest -x -q --tb=short; else echo "No test files yet — nothing to test."; fi'

# tests with the coverage gate (CI always runs this, not `test` — PI-569).
# without src/ yet, still run the plain test suite (tests/ may exist before
# src/ does) — only the coverage instrumentation/threshold is skipped, since
# 0% coverage on zero application code would trip --cov-fail-under before any
# code exists. Silently skipping pytest entirely here would let a real test
# failure through `just ci` unnoticed.
[doc("tests with the coverage gate (CI always runs this, not `test` — PI-569).")]
test-cov:
    sh -c 'if [ -d src ]; then uv run --with pytest-xdist --with pytest-cov pytest -n auto --tb=short -q --cov=src --cov-fail-under=70; elif find tests -type f \( -name "test_*.py" -o -name "*_test.py" \) 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then uv run --with pytest-xdist pytest -n auto --tb=short -q; else echo "No src/ or test files yet — nothing to test."; fi'

# mutation testing on core logic (slow; requires [tool.mutmut] source_paths
# in your own pyproject.toml, scoped to deterministic pure-logic modules —
# skip I/O-heavy code, hooks, template renderers). CI runs this nightly.
# Workers default to 1: mutmut forks os.cpu_count() workers, which a container
# reports as the HOST's count — 8 forks in a 1-CPU/1-GiB runner OOM-killed and
# then hung for 3h. Raise it per run: MUTMUT_MAX_CHILDREN=4 just test-mutation.
[doc("mutation testing on core logic")]
test-mutation:
    uv run --with mutmut mutmut run --max-children "${MUTMUT_MAX_CHILDREN:-1}"
    uv run --with mutmut mutmut export-cicd-stats

# dependency vulnerability scan against known CVEs/advisories (PI-568).
# complements admission_package.py, which only blocks installing a package that
# doesn't exist or looks typosquatted — this catches a real, correctly-
# spelled dependency with a known vulnerability already in the lockfile.
# It audits the exported lock, never an environment: `uv run --with pip-audit`
# scanned pip-audit's own dependencies too, and a stale certifi there held a
# project with none red for a week (PI-1111).
[doc("dependency vulnerability scan against known CVEs/advisories (PI-568).")]
audit:
    sh -c 'if [ -f pyproject.toml ] || [ -f uv.lock ]; then f="$(mktemp)" && uv export --all-extras --all-groups --no-emit-workspace --no-hashes -q > "$f" && uvx pip-audit --disable-pip --no-deps -r "$f"; rc=$?; rm -f "$f"; exit "$rc"; elif [ -f requirements.txt ]; then uvx pip-audit -r requirements.txt; else echo "No Python dependency manifest yet — nothing to audit."; fi'

# generate a CycloneDX SBOM of the runtime dependency tree (#574). release.yml
# attaches this to GitHub Releases; run locally on demand. --no-dev so it
# reflects what ships; uvx keeps cyclonedx-py out of the scanned .venv.
[doc("generate a CycloneDX SBOM of the runtime dependency tree (#574)")]
sbom:
    uv sync --no-dev
    uvx --from cyclonedx-bom cyclonedx-py environment .venv -o sbom.cdx.json

# dependency license compliance scan (#579) — fail on copyleft (GPL/AGPL; also
# LGPL, since --partial-match is substring-based). Tune the --fail-on deny-list
# to your policy. Non-blocking in CI initially (see ci.yml's license-scan job).
[doc("dependency license compliance scan (#579)")]
license:
    uv run --with pip-licenses pip-licenses --from=mixed --fail-on "GPL;AGPL" --partial-match

# property-based tests with Hypothesis (#580). Property tests are opt-in per file
# (import hypothesis); this recipe makes Hypothesis available without adding it as
# a permanent dependency. Pattern/tooling, NOT a blocking gate: CI runs this in
# the nightly `fuzz` job, never on a PR (#727). Hypothesis draws fresh seeds each
# run, so the nightly job explores inputs a per-PR run would only repeat.
[doc("property-based tests with Hypothesis (#580)")]
fuzz:
    uv run --with hypothesis --with pytest-xdist pytest -n auto --tb=short -q

# the naming standard over this repo, as a ratchet: new findings fail, a fixed
# finding must be deleted from gates/naming.baseline. Judges with the vendored package in
# vendor/naming/ (no checkout of the standard needed); UNCHECKED exits 3, never a pass. Guarded so
# an upgrade that declined the `naming-gate` addition group keeps a working `just lint`.
[doc("naming standard ratchet (gates/naming-check.sh)")]
naming:
    sh -c 'if [ -f gates/naming-check.sh ]; then sh gates/naming-check.sh; else echo "naming gate not installed here (project-init upgrade --apply --accept-new naming-gate)"; fi'

# docs front matter and generated-file headers (kind, owner, status; generated-by equals contracts/fresh-checks.tsv).
# Born warn: findings print and exit 0; `sh gates/doc-check.sh --strict` makes them red. Guarded like `naming`.
[doc("docs front matter + generated headers (gates/doc-check.sh)")]
docs-check:
    sh -c 'if [ -f gates/doc-check.sh ]; then sh gates/doc-check.sh; else echo "doc gate not installed here (project-init upgrade --apply --accept-new naming-gate)"; fi'

# what CI runs (the full gate)
ci: setup lint typecheck test-cov audit

# fast local gate for the pre-push hook: lint + parallel tests (CI is the full
# backstop, so pre-push stays fast and doesn't re-run typecheck/coverage/audit)
[doc("fast local gate for the pre-push hook")]
fast-ci: lint test

# route CI to a self-hosted runner when Actions minutes run out (PI-666);
# requires a registered runner — see .agents/docs/guides/self-hosted-ci-runner.md

# mypy.ini — static type checking gates for project code (scaffolded by project-init).
# ruff lints; it does not type-check. `just typecheck` runs this against src/
# only — test code and agent infra (.agents/**) are out of scope by construction,
# the same way ruff.toml exempts them via per-file-ignores.
#
# python_version pins the typeshed/syntax baseline mypy checks against. It is
# the same value as mise.toml's python pin and the CI matrix floor (#628); keep
# all three aligned with your pyproject.toml's requires-python floor.
#
# Deliberately NOT enabled: disallow_any_explicit / disallow_any_decorated.
# Verified against real code (PI-570) — both fire on legitimate, idiomatic
# `Any` (a JSON-parsing return type, `Callable[..., Any]` wrappers), not just
# lazy typing. `strict = True` already covers the flags with a good
# signal-to-noise ratio; these two are a net loss.

strict = True

# ruff.toml — quality gates for project code (scaffolded by project-init).
# Prefer pyproject.toml [tool.ruff]? Merge this in and delete the file —
# a root ruff.toml takes precedence over pyproject.toml.

line-length = 100
extend-exclude = [".claude"]

[lint]
# D       enforced docstrings (Google style)
# C901    cyclomatic complexity cap
# PLR091x branch/argument/statement caps
# RUF     ruff-native rules (e.g. mutable class defaults)
# PERF    performance anti-patterns (e.g. manual accumulation loops)
# PTH     use pathlib over os.path
# RET     return-statement clarity (dead assignments, needless else)
# ARG     unused arguments
# A       builtin shadowing
# S       bandit-derived security checks — cheap and instant, complements
#         Semgrep's CI-only SAST rather than duplicating it (PI-570)
# BLE     no blind `except Exception`/`except:` without a documented reason
#         (silence it deliberately with `# noqa: BLE001 — <why>`, not by omission)
# Together these stop "noodly" generated code mechanically — prose rules in
# CLAUDE.md decay; lint gates do not.
#
# Deliberately NOT selected: TRY (exception-handling style) and PL's broader
# pylint ports beyond PLR091x — evaluated and found to mostly re-flag patterns
# the groups above already catch, at a higher false-positive cost (PI-570).
select = [
    "E", "F", "W", "I", "N", "UP", "B", "SIM", "D", "C901",
    "PLR0912", "PLR0913", "PLR0915", "RUF", "PERF", "PTH", "RET", "ARG", "A", "S", "BLE",
]
ignore = ["E501"]
# DOC rules (pydoclint port: docstring/signature consistency) are still in
# preview — enable here once stable, or run standalone pydoclint until then:
# https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/12434

[lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[lint.mccabe]
# >10 usually means the function wants splitting.
max-complexity = 10

[lint.isort]
# The root conftest.py (the test contract) makes ruff resolve `conftest` to itself
# and call it first-party, which re-sorts every test importing a helper from
# tests/conftest.py. Pinned where it sorted before the contract existed.
known-third-party = ["conftest"]

[lint.per-file-ignores]
# Test names are self-describing; docstring enforcement adds noise not value.
# S: plain `assert` and fixture-only secrets are the point of a test, not a
# vulnerability (PI-570).
"tests/**" = ["D", "S"]
# Agent infrastructure (hooks/scripts) is not project code.
".agents/**" = ["D", "C901", "PLR0912", "PLR0913", "PLR0915"]

#!/usr/bin/env sh
# doc-fresh-verify.sh (harbor#1287) — is every generated file current? One verdict line per file, and the exact fix for a stale one.
#
#   sh bin/doc-fresh-verify.sh [--table FILE] [--root DIR]    exit 0 all fresh (or skipped/unchecked), 1 any stale, 2 usage
#
# WHY. 7 of 12 failed PR runs 2026-10-14..17 were a stale generated file (docs/generated/status.md, docs/context-map.md, a derived
# register or CODEOWNERS block), each found only after the 15-20 min suite pool. Every one of them has a generator
# --check that answers in seconds. The files and their checks are contracts/fresh-checks.tsv; the checks run in parallel,
# so the wall time is the slowest one (docs-gen, ~11 s), not the sum.
#
# A check that exits other than 0 or 1 could not judge (no python3, no git): UNCHECKED is a WARN line and does not fail, since
# a false red here is a push nobody can make. Skipped rows have nothing to judge in this tree (an export has no dev layer).
set -eu
case "$0" in */*) SRC="${0%/*}" ;; *) SRC=. ;; esac
. "$SRC/library-log.sh"
log_init fresh-check
_up=..; case "$(CDPATH= cd -- "$SRC" && pwd)" in */vendor/naming) _up=../.. ;; esac   # vendored: the repo is two levels up (harbor#1434)
ROOT="${HARBOR_SCOPE_ROOT:-$(CDPATH= cd -- "$SRC/$_up" && pwd)}"
TABLE=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --table) [ $# -ge 2 ] || { echo "fresh-check: --table needs a file" >&2; exit 2; }; TABLE="$2"; shift ;;
    --root) [ $# -ge 2 ] || { echo "fresh-check: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift ;;
    -h|--help) awk 'NR<2{next} /^#/{ sub(/^# ?/,""); if ($0=="") exit; print; next } {exit}' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "fresh-check: unknown argument $1 (sh $0 --help)" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  shift
done
[ -n "$TABLE" ] || TABLE="$ROOT/contracts/fresh-checks.tsv"
[ -f "$TABLE" ] || { echo "fresh-check: no table at $TABLE" >&2; exit 2; }
cd "$ROOT"
OUT="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fresh-check.XXXXXX")" || exit 2
trap 'rm -rf "$OUT"' EXIT

TAB="$(printf '\t')"; n=0
while IFS="$TAB" read -r f chk fix needs; do
  case "$f" in ''|\#*|-) continue ;; esac
  n=$((n + 1)); needs="${needs:-$f}"
  printf '%s\n' "$f" > "$OUT/$n.file"; printf '%s\n' "$fix" > "$OUT/$n.fix"
  if [ ! -e "$needs" ] && ! git ls-files --error-unmatch -- "$needs" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo skip > "$OUT/$n.rc"; continue
  fi
  ( rc=0; HARBOR_DOC_IN_FRESH_CHECK=1 sh -c "$chk" > "$OUT/$n.out" 2>&1 || rc=$?; echo "$rc" > "$OUT/$n.rc" ) &
done < "$TABLE"
wait

stale=0; i=1
while [ "$i" -le "$n" ]; do
  f="$(cat "$OUT/$i.file")"; rc="$(cat "$OUT/$i.rc" 2>/dev/null || echo 255)"
  case "$rc" in
    0)    log_ok "$f is current" ;;
    skip) log_skip "$f: nothing to judge in this tree" ;;
    1)    stale=$((stale + 1)); log_fail "$f is STALE"; log_fix "$(cat "$OUT/$i.fix")" ;;
    *)    log_warn "$f UNCHECKED: the check exited $rc ($(grep -v '^$' "$OUT/$i.out" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | cut -c1-120))" ;;
  esac
  i=$((i + 1))
done
log_end || :
[ "$stale" -eq 0 ] || { echo "fresh-check: $stale generated file(s) STALE: run each fix above, commit, push." >&2; exit 1; }

#!/usr/bin/env sh
# doc-shape.sh (harbor#1434, #1435) — every doc carries one front matter shape, every generated file one header.
#
#   sh bin/doc-shape.sh                 judge both halves
#   sh bin/doc-shape.sh --docs          only docs/**/*.md front matter (doc.kind-folder, doc.frontmatter-fields)
#   sh bin/doc-shape.sh --generated     only the generated-by header <-> contracts/fresh-checks.tsv row equality (doc.fresh-registered)
#   sh bin/doc-shape.sh --write         write the missing front matter into docs/**/*.md; idempotent; prints the files whose
#                                       owner fell back to the CODEOWNERS default as `default-owner TAB path`
#   sh bin/doc-shape.sh --list-generated   every file carrying the header, with its command
#
#   --root <dir>        the tree to judge (default: the repo this script sits in, or holds vendor/naming/)
#   --registry <dir>    kinds.tsv and controls.tsv (default <root>/standards/naming, else <root>/vendor/naming/registry)
#   --repo <name>       the repo name a bare ticket number is prefixed with (default: the origin remote's name)
#   --strict            exit 1 on any finding, whatever controls.tsv says (what a fixture proves red with)
#   --format findings   also print one `A|V TAB <id> TAB <path>` record per finding on stdout
#
# THE SHAPE. A doc's front matter carries kind (the kinds.tsv row whose folder holds the file, or a row of
# contracts/doc-folders.tsv), owner (`repo#n`, `KEY-n` or `@login`), status, and source where the kind's required_fields name
# it. A generated file carries `generated-by: <command>` in a comment of its own syntax; the command is the `fix` column of its
# contracts/fresh-checks.tsv row, and the two are held equal both ways. OWNER IS NEVER INVENTED: --write takes it from
# the doc's own owner_issue, a ticket in its title or source, the git history's top human author, then the CODEOWNERS default.
#   exit 0 clean, or only warn findings · 1 a block finding, or --strict · 2 usage · 3 unchecked
set -eu
LC_ALL=C; export LC_ALL
case "$0" in */*) SRC="${0%/*}" ;; *) SRC=. ;; esac
SRC="$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$SRC" && pwd -P)"
SELF="$SRC/$(basename -- "$0")"
# shellcheck disable=SC2034 # LOG_FD: read by library-log.sh
LOG_FD=2
. "$SRC/library-log.sh"
log_init doc-shape

usage() { awk 'NR < 2 { next } /^# THE SHAPE/ || !/^#/ { exit } { sub(/^# ?/, ""); print }' "$SELF"; }
usage_err() { log_fail "$1"; log_fix "sh $SELF --help"; log_end || :; exit 2; }
unchecked() { log_fail "$1"; log_fix "$2"; log_end || :; exit 3; }

ACTION=judge; HALF=all; ROOT=""; REG=""; REPO=""; STRICT=0; FORMAT=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    --docs) HALF=docs ;;
    --generated) HALF=generated ;;
    --write) ACTION=write ;;
    --list-generated) ACTION=list ;;
    --strict) STRICT=1 ;;
    --root) [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage_err "--root needs a directory"; ROOT="$2"; shift ;;
    --registry) [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage_err "--registry needs a directory"; REG="$2"; shift ;;
    --repo) [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage_err "--repo needs a name"; REPO="$2"; shift ;;
    --format) [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage_err "--format needs a value"; FORMAT="$2"; shift ;;
    -*) usage_err "unknown option $1" ;;
    *) usage_err "unexpected argument $1" ;;
  esac
  shift
done
case "$FORMAT" in ''|findings) ;; *) usage_err "--format is findings" ;; esac
if [ -z "$ROOT" ]; then
  # sitting in vendor/naming/, the repo is two levels up
  ROOT="$SRC/.."; case "$SRC" in */vendor/naming) ROOT="$SRC/../.." ;; esac
fi
ROOT="$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$ROOT" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || usage_err "--root is not a directory"
if [ -z "$REG" ]; then
  if [ -f "$ROOT/standards/naming/kinds.tsv" ]; then REG="$ROOT/standards/naming"; else REG="$ROOT/vendor/naming/registry"; fi
fi
KINDS="$REG/kinds.tsv"; CONTROLS="$REG/controls.tsv"
OVR="$ROOT/contracts/doc-folders.tsv"; FRESH="$ROOT/contracts/fresh-checks.tsv"
T="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/doc-shape.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT INT TERM HUP
TAB="$(printf '\t')"
# the header, in each comment syntax: `# generated-by: cmd`, `// generated-by: cmd`, `<!-- generated-by: cmd -->`
HDR_RE='^(#|//|;|--|<!--) ?generated-by: ?[^ ]'

# mode_of <id> → shadow | warn | block (warn when the registry has no row: a vendored copy may predate the control)
mode_of() {
  [ -f "$CONTROLS" ] || { echo warn; return 0; }
  _m="$(awk -F'\t' -v id="$1" '/^#/ { next } $1 == id { m = $2; if (m == "advisory" || m == "inform") m = "warn"; print m; exit }' "$CONTROLS")"
  echo "${_m:-warn}"
}

# ── the docs ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# scan_docs → `path TAB expected-kind TAB fm TAB kind TAB owner TAB status TAB source TAB gen TAB owner_issue` per doc.
scan_docs() {
  [ -d "$ROOT/docs" ] || return 0
  (cd "$ROOT" && find docs -type f -name '*.md' | LC_ALL=C sort) > "$T/doclist"
  awk -F'\t' -v ROOT="$ROOT" -v KINDS="$KINDS" -v OVR="$OVR" -v LIST="$T/doclist" -v HDR="$HDR_RE" '
  function trim(s) { sub(/^[ \t\r]+/, "", s); sub(/[ \t\r]+$/, "", s); return s }
  function nz(s) { return (s == "" ? "-" : s) }
  function unq(s) { s = trim(s); if (s ~ /^".*"$/ || s ~ /^\047.*\047$/) s = substr(s, 2, length(s) - 2); return s }
  function expected(p,   i, best, bl, f, n, seg) {
    best = ""; bl = 0
    for (i = 1; i <= nf; i++) {
      f = FOLDER[i]
      if (substr(f, length(f)) == "/") { if (substr(p, 1, length(f)) == f && length(f) > bl) { best = FKIND[i]; bl = length(f) } }
      else if (p == f) { best = FKIND[i]; bl = 9999 }
    }
    if (best == "") { n = split(p, seg, "/"); if (n == 2 && (seg[2] == "README.md" || seg[2] == "index.md")) best = "reference" }
    return best
  }
  BEGIN {
    while ((getline l < KINDS) > 0) {
      if (l ~ /^#/ || l ~ /^[ \t]*$/) continue
      n = split(l, c, "\t")
      if (c[1] == "id" || n < 5) continue
      if (c[2] ~ /^docs\//) { nf++; FOLDER[nf] = c[2]; FKIND[nf] = c[1] }
    }
    close(KINDS)
    while ((getline l < OVR) > 0) {
      if (l ~ /^#/ || l ~ /^[ \t]*$/) continue
      n = split(l, c, "\t")
      if (c[1] == "folder" || n < 2) continue
      nf++; FOLDER[nf] = c[1]; FKIND[nf] = c[2]
    }
    close(OVR)
    while ((getline p < LIST) > 0) {
      fm = 0; kind = owner = status = source = oi = ""; gen = 0; ln = 0; inf = 0; done = 0
      path = ROOT "/" p
      while ((getline line < path) > 0) {
        ln++
        sub(/\r$/, "", line)
        if (line ~ HDR) gen = 1
        if (ln == 1) { if (line == "---") { inf = 1; fm = 1 } ; if (inf) continue }
        if (inf && !done) {
          if (line == "---") { inf = 0; done = 1; continue }
          if (line ~ /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:/) {
            k = substr(line, 1, index(line, ":") - 1); v = unq(substr(line, index(line, ":") + 1))
            if (k == "kind") kind = v; else if (k == "owner") owner = v; else if (k == "status") status = v
            else if (k == "source") source = v; else if (k == "owner_issue") oi = v
          }
        }
      }
      close(path)
      # an empty field is "-": tab is IFS whitespace for `read`, which would fold two empty fields into none
      printf "%s\t%s\t%d\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%s\n", p, nz(expected(p)), fm, nz(kind), nz(owner), nz(status), nz(source), gen, nz(oi)
    }
  }' /dev/null
}

# judge_docs <docs.tsv> → `id TAB path TAB message`
judge_docs() {
  awk -F'\t' -v KINDS="$KINDS" '
  BEGIN {
    while ((getline l < KINDS) > 0) {
      if (l ~ /^#/ || l ~ /^[ \t]*$/) continue
      n = split(l, c, "\t"); if (c[1] == "id" || n < 5) continue
      REQ[c[1]] = " " c[5] " "
    }
    close(KINDS)
    nstat = split("proposed accepted rejected superseded current draft unreviewed archived generated", S, " ")
    for (i = 1; i <= nstat; i++) OK[S[i]] = 1
  }
  {
    for (i = 2; i <= 9; i++) if ($i == "-") $i = ""
    p = $1; ex = $2; fm = $3; kind = $4; owner = $5; status = $6; source = $7; gen = $8
    if (ex == "") { print "doc.kind-folder\t" p "\tno kind is declared for this folder: add a row to contracts/doc-folders.tsv"; next }
    if (!fm) { print "doc.frontmatter-fields\t" p "\tno front matter: needs kind " ex ", owner and status (sh bin/doc-shape.sh --write)"; next }
    if (kind == "") print "doc.frontmatter-fields\t" p "\tfront matter has no kind (this folder holds " ex ")"
    else if (kind != ex) print "doc.kind-folder\t" p "\tkind is " kind " but this folder holds " ex
    if (owner == "") print "doc.frontmatter-fields\t" p "\tfront matter has no owner (a ticket repo#n or KEY-n, or a person @login)"
    else if (owner !~ /^@[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*$/ && owner !~ /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*#[0-9]+$/ && owner !~ /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9]+$/)
      print "doc.frontmatter-fields\t" p "\towner " owner " is neither a ticket (repo#n, KEY-n) nor a person (@login)"
    if (status == "") print "doc.frontmatter-fields\t" p "\tfront matter has no status"
    else if (!(status in OK)) print "doc.frontmatter-fields\t" p "\tstatus " status " is not one of: proposed accepted rejected superseded current draft unreviewed archived generated"
    if (index(REQ[ex], " source ") && source == "") print "doc.frontmatter-fields\t" p "\t" ex " needs a source (the command or file it derives from)"
    if (index(REQ[ex], " generated-by ") && !gen) print "doc.frontmatter-fields\t" p "\t" ex " needs a generated-by header (standards/naming.md, document header)"
  }' "$1"
}

# ── the generated header ↔ fresh-checks.tsv ─────────────────────────────────
# scan_headers → `path TAB command` per file carrying the header (first header of a file wins)
scan_headers() {
  : > "$T/hits"
  if git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" = "$ROOT" ]; then
    git -C "$ROOT" grep -I -n -E "$HDR_RE" -- . ':!fixtures/' ':!tests/' ':!vendor/skills/' ':!vendor/skills-archive/' ':!vendor/archify/' ':!evals/' > "$T/hits" 2>/dev/null || :
  else
    ( cd "$ROOT" && grep -r -I -n -E "$HDR_RE" . --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=fixtures --exclude-dir=tests --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.worktrees 2>/dev/null ) | sed 's|^\./||' > "$T/hits" || :
  fi
  awk -F':' '
    { p = $1; ln = $2; rest = $0; sub(/^[^:]*:[^:]*:/, "", rest)
      if (ln + 0 > 20 || p in seen) next   # a header sits in the first 20 lines: a generator that prints one holds the literal further down
      seen[p] = 1
      c = rest; sub(/^(#|\/\/|;|--|<!--) ?generated-by: ?/, "", c); sub(/[ \t]*-->[ \t]*$/, "", c); sub(/[ \t\r]+$/, "", c)
      printf "%s\t%s\n", p, c }' "$T/hits" | LC_ALL=C sort
}

# judge_generated <headers.tsv> → `id TAB path TAB message`
judge_generated() {
  : > "$T/rows"
  [ ! -f "$FRESH" ] || awk -F'\t' '/^#/ || $1 == "" || $1 == "-" { next } { print $1 "\t" $3 "\t" (($4 == "") ? $1 : $4) }' "$FRESH" > "$T/rows"
  awk -F'\t' -v ROOT="$ROOT" '
  function present(p,   cmd, rc) { cmd = "test -e \"" ROOT "/" p "\""; rc = system(cmd); return rc == 0 }
  FILENAME == HDRS { H[$1] = $2; next }
  { R[$1] = $2; RN[$1] = $3 }
  END {
    for (p in H) {
      if (!(p in R)) print "doc.fresh-registered\t" p "\tcarries generated-by: " H[p] " but contracts/fresh-checks.tsv has no row for it"
      else if (R[p] != H[p]) print "doc.fresh-registered\t" p "\tgenerated-by says [" H[p] "] but its fresh-checks.tsv fix is [" R[p] "]"
    }
    for (p in R) {
      if (p in H) continue
      if (!present(p) && !present(RN[p])) continue
      if (present(p)) print "doc.fresh-registered\t" p "\thas a contracts/fresh-checks.tsv row but no generated-by header"
    }
  }' HDRS="$1" "$1" "$T/rows"
}

# report <findings.tsv> → logs each, records them, returns 1 when the run must fail
report() {
  _bad=0
  LC_ALL=C sort -u "$1" > "$T/f.sorted"
  while IFS="$TAB" read -r _id _p _msg; do
    [ -n "$_id" ] || continue
    _m="$(mode_of "$_id")"
    [ -z "${LINT_REDLOG:-}" ] || printf '%s\n' "$_id" >> "$LINT_REDLOG" 2>/dev/null || :
    [ "$_m" != shadow ] || continue
    if [ "$FORMAT" = findings ]; then printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$( [ "$_m" = block ] && echo V || echo A)" "$_id" "$_p"; fi
    if [ "$_m" = block ] || [ "$STRICT" = 1 ]; then log_fail "[$_id] $_p — $_msg"; log_nofix "contracts/doc-folders.tsv, or sh $SELF --write"; _bad=1
    else log_warn "[$_id] $_p — $_msg"; fi
  done < "$T/f.sorted"
  [ "$_bad" -eq 0 ]
}

if [ "$ACTION" = list ]; then
  scan_headers | awk -F'\t' '{ printf "%s\t%s\n", $1, $2 }'
  exit 0
fi

# ── apply ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# default_owner → the CODEOWNERS default: the `*` rule's first owner, else the owner named most often
default_owner() {
  for _c in "$ROOT/.github/CODEOWNERS" "$ROOT/CODEOWNERS" "$ROOT/docs/CODEOWNERS"; do
    [ -f "$_c" ] || continue
    awk '/^#/ || NF < 2 { next }
      $1 == "*" { for (i = 2; i <= NF; i++) if ($i ~ /^@/) { print $i; found = 1; exit } }
      { for (i = 2; i <= NF; i++) if ($i ~ /^@/) n[$i]++ }
      END { if (found) exit; for (o in n) if (n[o] > best || (n[o] == best && o < top)) { best = n[o]; top = o } if (top != "") print top }' "$_c" && return 0
  done
  return 1
}

# the repo name a bare #n belongs to
repo_name() {
  [ -z "$REPO" ] || { printf '%s' "$REPO"; return 0; }
  _u="$(git -C "$ROOT" remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null || true)"
  _u="${_u##*/}"; _u="${_u%.git}"
  printf '%s' "${_u:-$(basename "$ROOT")}"
}

# author_logins → key TAB login, the key a commit author's name or address: a login can be read only off a noreply address,
# so the same person's other addresses are matched through the name they committed under
author_logins() {
  git -C "$ROOT" log --format='%an%x09%ae' 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort -u | awk -F'\t' '
    $1 ~ /\[bot\]$/ { next }
    { N[NR] = $1; E[NR] = $2; n = NR
      if ($2 ~ /^[0-9]+\+[A-Za-z0-9-]+@users\.noreply\.github\.com$/) { l = $2; sub(/^[0-9]+\+/, "", l); sub(/@.*/, "", l); L[$1] = l } }
    END { for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (N[i] in L) { print N[i] "\t" L[N[i]]; print E[i] "\t" L[N[i]] } }' | LC_ALL=C sort -u
}

# git_owner <path> → @login of the commit author with most commits to the path (bots excluded), or nothing
git_owner() {
  git -C "$ROOT" log --follow --format='%an%x09%ae' -- "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' -v MAP="$T/logins" '
    BEGIN { while ((getline l < MAP) > 0) { split(l, c, "\t"); M[c[1]] = c[2] } }
    $1 ~ /\[bot\]$/ || $2 ~ /noreply@anthropic\.com$/ { next }
    { lg = ""
      if ($2 ~ /^[0-9]+\+[A-Za-z0-9-]+@users\.noreply\.github\.com$/) { lg = $2; sub(/^[0-9]+\+/, "", lg); sub(/@.*/, "", lg) }
      else if ($2 in M) lg = M[$2]
      else if ($1 in M) lg = M[$1]
      if (lg != "") n[lg]++ }
    END { for (o in n) if (n[o] > best || (n[o] == best && o < top)) { best = n[o]; top = o } if (top != "") print "@" top }'
}

# ticket_owner <path> <owner_issue> <source> → repo#n or nothing: the doc'"'"'s own words, never a guess
ticket_owner() {
  _oi="$2"; _src="$3"
  case "$_oi" in
    ''|*[!0-9]*) ;;
    *) printf '%s#%s' "$RNAME" "$_oi"; return 0 ;;
  esac
  case "$_oi" in *#[0-9]*) printf '%s' "$_oi"; return 0 ;; esac
  case "$_src" in [A-Za-z]*#[0-9]*) case "$_src" in *[!A-Za-z0-9._#-]*) ;; *) printf '%s' "$_src"; return 0 ;; esac ;; esac
  _title="$(awk 'NR == 1 && $0 == "---" { fm = 1; next } fm && $0 == "---" { fm = 0; next } fm { next } /^# / { print; exit }' "$ROOT/$1")"
  _t="$(printf '%s\n' "$_title" | grep -oE '[A-Za-z0-9._-]+#[0-9]+|\(#[0-9]+\)' | head -n 1 || true)"
  case "$_t" in
    '') ;;
    '(#'*) _t="${_t#(#}"; printf '%s#%s' "$RNAME" "${_t%)}"; return 0 ;;
    *) printf '%s' "$_t"; return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}

# fm_block <kind> <owner> <status> <source> → the lines to add
apply_one() { # <path> <expected> <fm> <kind> <owner> <status> <source> <gen> <oi>
  _p="$1"; _ex="$2"; _fm="$3"; _kd="$4"; _ow="$5"; _st="$6"; _sr="$7"; _oi="$9"
  [ -n "$_ex" ] || { printf 'unmapped\t%s\n' "$_p"; return 0; }
  : > "$T/add"
  [ -n "$_kd" ] || printf 'kind: %s\n' "$_ex" >> "$T/add"
  if [ -z "$_ow" ]; then
    _o=""
    _o="$(ticket_owner "$_p" "$_oi" "$_sr" || true)"
    [ -n "$_o" ] || _o="$(git_owner "$_p" || true)"
    if [ -z "$_o" ]; then _o="$DEFAULT_OWNER"; printf 'default-owner\t%s\n' "$_p"; fi
    printf 'owner: %s\n' "$_o" >> "$T/add"
  fi
  if [ -z "$_st" ]; then
    _s=unreviewed
    case "$_ex" in generated-doc|context-map) _s=generated ;; esac
    case "$_ex:$_p" in decision-record:*/README.md|decision-record:*/index.md) ;; decision-record:*)   # an ADR states its own status in its body
      _b="$(sed -n '1,15p' "$ROOT/$_p" | sed -n 's/^[-*_ ]*[Ss]tatus[*_]*:[*_ ]*\([A-Za-z]*\).*/\1/p' | head -n 1 | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')"
      case "$_b" in proposed|accepted|rejected|superseded) _s="$_b" ;; esac ;;
    esac
    printf 'status: %s\n' "$_s" >> "$T/add"
  fi
  if [ -z "$_sr" ] && awk -F'\t' -v k="$_ex" '$1 == k && (" " $5 " ") ~ / source / { f = 1 } END { exit !f }' "$KINDS" 2>/dev/null; then
    _f="$(awk -F'\t' -v p="$_p" '$1 == p { print $2; exit }' "$T/rows" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [ -z "$_f" ] || printf 'source: %s\n' "$_f" >> "$T/add"
  fi
  [ -s "$T/add" ] || return 0
  if [ "$_fm" = 1 ]; then
    awk -v ADD="$T/add" 'NR == 1 { print; next } !done && $0 == "---" { while ((getline l < ADD) > 0) print l; done = 1 } { print }' "$ROOT/$_p" > "$T/new"
  else
    { printf -- '---\n'; cat "$T/add"; printf -- '---\n\n'; cat "$ROOT/$_p"; } > "$T/new"
  fi
  cat "$T/new" > "$ROOT/$_p"
  printf 'wrote\t%s\n' "$_p"
}

if [ "$ACTION" = write ]; then
  [ -f "$KINDS" ] || unchecked "no kinds.tsv at $KINDS, so no folder has a kind" "ls $REG"
  RNAME="$(repo_name)"
  DEFAULT_OWNER="$(default_owner || true)"
  [ -n "$DEFAULT_OWNER" ] || unchecked "no CODEOWNERS file names an owner, so a doc with no derivable owner would get none" "add .github/CODEOWNERS"
  author_logins > "$T/logins"
  scan_docs > "$T/docs.tsv"
  : > "$T/rows"; [ ! -f "$FRESH" ] || awk -F'\t' '/^#/ || $1 == "" || $1 == "-" { next } { print $1 "\t" $3 }' "$FRESH" > "$T/rows"
  while IFS="$TAB" read -r p ex fm kd ow st sr gen oi; do
    [ "$ex" != - ] || ex=""; [ "$kd" != - ] || kd=""; [ "$ow" != - ] || ow=""; [ "$st" != - ] || st=""; [ "$sr" != - ] || sr=""; [ "$oi" != - ] || oi=""
    apply_one "$p" "$ex" "$fm" "$kd" "$ow" "$st" "$sr" "$gen" "$oi"
  done < "$T/docs.tsv" > "$T/applied"
  _w="$(grep -c '^wrote' "$T/applied" || true)"
  grep -E '^(default-owner|unmapped)' "$T/applied" || :
  log_ok "wrote front matter into $_w doc(s); $(grep -c '^default-owner' "$T/applied" || true) took the default owner $DEFAULT_OWNER"
  log_end || :
  exit 0
fi

# ── judge ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
: > "$T/findings"
if [ "$HALF" = all ] || [ "$HALF" = docs ]; then
  [ -f "$KINDS" ] || unchecked "no kinds.tsv at $KINDS, so no folder has a kind" "ls $REG"
  scan_docs > "$T/docs.tsv"
  judge_docs "$T/docs.tsv" >> "$T/findings"
  _nd="$(grep -c . "$T/docs.tsv" || true)"
fi
if [ "$HALF" = all ] || [ "$HALF" = generated ]; then
  scan_headers > "$T/headers.tsv"
  judge_generated "$T/headers.tsv" >> "$T/findings"
  _ng="$(grep -c . "$T/headers.tsv" || true)"
fi
_rc=0
report "$T/findings" || _rc=1
if [ ! -s "$T/findings" ]; then
  [ -z "${_nd:-}" ] || log_ok "$_nd doc(s) carry the front matter shape"
  [ -z "${_ng:-}" ] || log_ok "${_ng} generated file(s) carry the header, each with its fresh-checks.tsv row"
fi
log_end || :
exit "$_rc"
vendor/naming/library-log.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env sh
# library-log.sh (harbor#771) — the one log format (contracts/logging.md), sourced by every tool that logs.
# Never run: it sets no shell option (set -u in a sourced file would leak into every caller), and
# every function is safe under the caller's set -eu.
#
#   . "$HERE/library-log.sh"
#   log_init <tool>               name the run and zero the counters (default: the script's name)
#   log_file <target>             opt in: the same lines, timestamped, in <target>/backups/<tool>/<TS>/log
#   log_head <step>               ── <tool> · <step>
#   log_ok|log_fail|log_warn|log_note|log_skip <message>      "  <TAG>: <message>"
#   log_fix <command>             "  fix: <command>" — the command that resolves the FAIL above
#   log_nofix <issue-or-doc>      "  fix: none automatic — see <issue-or-doc>"
#   pkg_hint <tool>               the command that installs <tool> on THIS machine (brew on macOS; apt-get, dnf, pacman, apk or
#                                 zypper on Linux/WSL2), for `log_fix "$(pkg_hint jq)"`. Prints one line, exits 0, never installs
#   log_end                       "<tool>: N ok, M failed, K warnings", then "log: <path>"; returns 0 iff M is 0
#   log_receipt <dir> <id> <status> [subject...]   a check's receipt for the finding ledger (harbor#896)
#   receipt_dir [config-dir]      the one receipt dir a writer passes to log_receipt and the reconcile reads
#   slug_of_url <url>             owner/name of a github.com remote (https, git@ or ssh spelling), nothing for any other URL
#   slug_valid <owner/name>       0 when it is exactly two github-shaped segments
#   repo_slug [dir]               owner/name of the repository THIS harbor is, for the script in <dir> (default: the caller's own
#                                 dir); nothing when none is derivable. Never fails the caller (harbor#1149)
#   status_init <id> [config-dir] begin a `<check> --status` report (contracts/reconcile.md, harbor#1031)
#   status_ok | status_drift <key> <desired> <observed> [delta] | status_unjudged <reason> | status_end
#                                 one item at its desired state / not at it / the run could not judge / close the report
#
# LOG_FD=2 sends the log to stderr, for a tool whose stdout is data. LOG_TS names the run dir when the
# caller already chose one. After log_file, LOG_DIR is the run dir (backups go beside the log) and
# LOG_PATH the file, empty when there is none.

# Sourced twice (a tool and a library it uses), the second source keeps the run's counts.
if [ -z "${_LOG_LIB:-}" ]; then
  _LOG_LIB=1
  _log_b="${0##*/}"; LOG_TOOL="${_log_b%.sh}"
  LOG_DIR=""; LOG_PATH=""; _LOG_WHY=""
  _LOG_OK=0; _LOG_FAILED=0; _LOG_WARNED=0; _LOG_NEEDFIX=0
fi

log_init() { # <tool>
  LOG_TOOL="${1:-$LOG_TOOL}"
  _LOG_OK=0; _LOG_FAILED=0; _LOG_WARNED=0; _LOG_NEEDFIX=0
}

# One line to the screen and, when there is one, to the file behind an ISO-8601 UTC time. A file
# that stops taking writes is said once on stderr and dropped; the screen never is.
_log_emit() { # <line>
  if [ "${LOG_FD:-1}" = 2 ]; then printf '%s\n' "$1" >&2 || :; else printf '%s\n' "$1" || :; fi
  [ -n "$LOG_PATH" ] || return 0
  if ! { printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$1" >> "$LOG_PATH"; } 2>/dev/null; then
    printf 'log-lib: %s stopped accepting writes — logging to the screen only\n' "$LOG_PATH" >&2
    _LOG_WHY="$LOG_PATH (incomplete — a write failed)"; LOG_PATH=""
  fi
  return 0
}

# A FAIL left without its fix is said, and counted, before the next line or the summary.
_log_needfix() {
  [ "$_LOG_NEEDFIX" = 1 ] || return 0
  _LOG_NEEDFIX=0; _LOG_WARNED=$((_LOG_WARNED + 1))
  _log_emit "  WARN: no fix line followed the FAIL above — $LOG_TOOL breaks contracts/logging.md"
  _log_emit "  fix: none automatic — see contracts/logging.md"
}

_log_line() { # <TAG> <message>
  _log_needfix
  _log_m="${2-}"
  case "$_log_m" in *'
'*) _log_m="$(printf '%s' "$_log_m" | tr '\n' ' ')" ;; esac
  if [ "$1" = '──' ]; then _log_emit "── $LOG_TOOL · $_log_m"; else _log_emit "  $1: $_log_m"; fi
}

log_head() { _log_line '──' "${1-}"; }
log_ok()   { _LOG_OK=$((_LOG_OK + 1)); _log_line ok "${1-}"; }
log_fail() { _log_line FAIL "${1-}"; _LOG_FAILED=$((_LOG_FAILED + 1)); _LOG_NEEDFIX=1; }
log_warn() { _LOG_WARNED=$((_LOG_WARNED + 1)); _log_line WARN "${1-}"; }
log_note() { _log_line note "${1-}"; }
log_skip() { _log_line skip "${1-}"; }
log_fix()  { _LOG_NEEDFIX=0; _log_emit "  fix: ${1-}"; }
log_nofix() { log_fix "none automatic — see ${1-}"; }

# pkg_hint (harbor#618): the install command a "tool is missing" FAIL should name on this OS. A tool's package
# name differs per manager (python3 is `python` on pacman, ShellCheck on dnf); one with no distro package
# (bun, gitleaks on apt/dnf) names its install page. With no known manager it still says what to install.
pkg_hint() { # <tool>
  _ph_t="${1-}"
  # A stripped PATH (a test, a hook) can lack uname; macOS and Linux both keep it in /usr/bin.
  _ph_os="$(uname -s 2>/dev/null || /usr/bin/uname -s 2>/dev/null || :)"
  case "$_ph_os" in
    Darwin)
      case "$_ph_t" in
        bun) printf 'brew install oven-sh/bun/bun\n' ;; python3) printf 'brew install python\n' ;;
        awk) printf 'brew install gawk\n' ;; sed) printf 'brew install gnu-sed\n' ;;
        mkfifo|sha256) printf 'brew install coreutils\n' ;; find) printf 'brew install findutils\n' ;;
        diff) printf 'brew install diffutils\n' ;; *) printf 'brew install %s\n' "$_ph_t" ;;
      esac; return 0 ;;
  esac
  case "$_ph_t" in bun) printf 'see https://bun.sh/docs/installation (bun has no distro package)\n'; return 0 ;; esac
  for _ph_m in apt-get dnf pacman apk zypper; do command -v "$_ph_m" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; _ph_m=""; done
  _ph_p="$_ph_t"
  case "$_ph_t:$_ph_m" in
    awk:*) _ph_p=gawk ;; mkfifo:*|sha256:*) _ph_p=coreutils ;; find:*) _ph_p=findutils ;; diff:*) _ph_p=diffutils ;;
    python3:pacman) _ph_p=python ;; python3:apk) _ph_p=python3 ;; shellcheck:dnf) _ph_p=ShellCheck ;;
    gh:pacman|gh:apk) _ph_p=github-cli ;;
    gitleaks:apt-get|gitleaks:dnf|gitleaks:zypper|gitleaks:)
      printf 'see https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases (no %s package)\n' "${_ph_m:-distro}"; return 0 ;;
  esac
  case "$_ph_m" in
    apt-get) printf 'sudo apt-get install -y %s\n' "$_ph_p" ;; dnf) printf 'sudo dnf install -y %s\n' "$_ph_p" ;;
    pacman) printf 'sudo pacman -S %s\n' "$_ph_p" ;; apk) printf 'sudo apk add %s\n' "$_ph_p" ;;
    zypper) printf 'sudo zypper install %s\n' "$_ph_p" ;;
    *) printf 'install %s with your distro package manager\n' "$_ph_p" ;;
  esac
}

log_file() { # <target>
  _log_ts="${LOG_TS:-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)}"
  _log_d="${1%/}/backups/$LOG_TOOL/$_log_ts"
  # A run in the same second as another gets its own dir rather than appending to that log.
  [ ! -e "$_log_d/log" ] || _log_d="$_log_d-$$"
  if mkdir -p "$_log_d" 2>/dev/null && : >> "$_log_d/log" 2>/dev/null; then
    LOG_DIR="$_log_d"; LOG_PATH="$_log_d/log"; _LOG_WHY=""
  else
    printf 'log-lib: could not create %s — logging to the screen only\n' "$_log_d" >&2
    # LOG_DIR is read by the caller, for its backups.
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034
    LOG_DIR=""; LOG_PATH=""; _LOG_WHY="none — could not create $_log_d"
  fi
  return 0
}

log_end() {
  _log_needfix
  _log_emit "$LOG_TOOL: $_LOG_OK ok, $_LOG_FAILED failed, $_LOG_WARNED warnings"
  if [ -n "$LOG_PATH" ]; then _log_emit "log: $LOG_PATH"
  elif [ -n "$_LOG_WHY" ]; then _log_emit "log: $_LOG_WHY"; fi
  [ "$_LOG_FAILED" -eq 0 ]
}

# ── the check tier's receipt (harbor#896, contracts/finding.md) ──────────────
#   log_receipt <dir> <id> <green|red|stood-down> [subject...]
# writes <dir>/<id>.json = {"id", "ran_at", "status", "subjects": [...]} atomically, and returns 1 when
# it could not, so the caller says so in its own log. `lint-findings.sh reconcile` reads it and never re-runs
# the check. Subjects are stable ids (a repo name, a path, a short sha), never a count or a date, which
# would move the digest on their own. No jq: a check that adopts it gains no dependency.
_receipt_json() { # <string> → a JSON string literal; control characters dropped
  printf '"%s"' "$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr -d '\000-\037' | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g')"
}
# The one receipt dir, for every writer and the reconcile (harbor#904): HARBOR_CHECK_RECEIPTS, else
# <config dir>/cache/checks. A writer's own cache dir (HARBOR_SCOPE_CACHE_DIR) never moves it.
receipt_dir() { printf '%s' "${HARBOR_CHECK_RECEIPTS:-${1:-${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}}/cache/checks}"; }
log_receipt() {
  [ "$#" -ge 3 ] || return 1
  _rd="$1"; _ri="$2"; _rs="$3"; shift 3
  case "$_rs" in green|red|stood-down) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  # Dots are in an id since harbor#1050 (`status.obligations`, as `event.retention` is) but never leading or doubled: the id
  # is a file name, and `.x` or `a..b` is not a name a reader's glob or a path check should be asked to trust.
  case "$_ri" in ''|.*|*..*|*.|*[!abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0-9.-]*) return 1 ;; esac
  mkdir -p "$_rd" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  _rl=""
  for _rj in "$@"; do
    [ -n "$_rj" ] || continue
    _rl="${_rl:+$_rl,}$(_receipt_json "$_rj")"
  done
  # mktemp, never a predictable name: the cache is session-writable, and a planted symlink would
  # aim this write at whatever it points to (review #895).
  _rt="$(mktemp "$_rd/.$_ri.json.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  # LOG_RECEIPT_FRESH_DAYS: how long the receipt counts as a run, for a check that runs less than
  # daily (harbor#577). Absent, the reconcile's default window applies.
  _rf=""; case "${LOG_RECEIPT_FRESH_DAYS:-}" in ''|*[!0-9]*) ;; *) _rf=",\"fresh_days\":$LOG_RECEIPT_FRESH_DAYS" ;; esac
  printf '{"id":%s,"ran_at":"%s","status":"%s","subjects":[%s]%s}\n' \
    "$(_receipt_json "$_ri")" "$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')" "$_rs" "$_rl" "$_rf" > "$_rt" 2>/dev/null \
    && mv -f "$_rt" "$_rd/$_ri.json" 2>/dev/null \
    || { rm -f "$_rt" 2>/dev/null; return 1; }
}

# ── this repository's own name (harbor#1149) ────────────────────────────────
# A tool that names harbor's own repository (the CI reads, the gate's fetch) asks here, so no script spells it and a clone
# under another owner targets itself. THE ORDER IS THE POINT:
#   1. <dir> sits in a harbor checkout (<dir>/../contracts/repo-slug.txt exists): that checkout's origin, read raw from its own
#      config (an insteadOf rewrite is not applied). A checkout with no github.com origin takes the pin of step 2.
#   2. <dir> is an install: <dir>/repo-slug.txt, which runtime-install ships from contracts/repo-slug.txt.
# NOTHING ELSE IS READ: not the environment, not the registered ~/port checkout, not the private layer. A session can write
# all three, and lint-findings-run.sh fetches and runs what this names with the operator's gh login (review #895): a name a
# session could redirect would be a fetch it could redirect. A tool's own override variable (HARBOR_CI_PLAN_REPO, ...) is its
# caller's decision, taken before it asks here.
slug_of_url() { # <url> — what the bootstrap installer and repo_slug share: the three spellings a clone is given, else nothing
  case "${1-}" in
    https://github.com/*)     _sg="${1#https://github.com/}" ;;
    git@github.com:*)         _sg="${1#git@github.com:}" ;;
    ssh://git@github.com/*)   _sg="${1#ssh://git@github.com/}" ;;
    *)                        return 0 ;;
  esac
  _sg="${_sg%/}"; printf '%s' "${_sg%.git}"
}
slug_valid() { # <owner/name> — exactly two segments, github's own alphabets, no leading dash or dot
  case "${1-}" in ''|*/*/*|/*|*/|-*|*/-*|*/.*|*[!A-Za-z0-9/._-]*) return 1 ;; */*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  case "${1%%/*}" in *[!A-Za-z0-9-]*) return 1 ;; esac
}
_rs_pin() { # <file> — its first line that is not blank or a # comment, when that line is a slug
  [ -f "$1" ] || return 0
  while IFS= read -r _rp_l || [ -n "$_rp_l" ]; do
    _rp_l="${_rp_l%"${_rp_l##*[![:space:]]}"}"
    case "$_rp_l" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
    if slug_valid "$_rp_l"; then printf '%s\n' "$_rp_l"; fi
    return 0
  done < "$1"
  return 0
}
repo_slug() { # [dir]
  _rs_d="${1:-}"
  if [ -z "$_rs_d" ]; then case "$0" in */*) _rs_d="${0%/*}" ;; *) _rs_d=. ;; esac; fi
  _rs_d="$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$_rs_d" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || return 0
  if [ -f "$_rs_d/../contracts/repo-slug.txt" ]; then
    # An empty environment but PATH, and only the checkout's own config: a hook's GIT_DIR would answer for the repository that is
    # committing, a GIT_TRACE would write a file, and a global config is not the checkout's origin.
    _rs_u="$(env -i "PATH=$PATH" git -C "$_rs_d/.." config --local --get remote.origin.url 2>/dev/null)" || _rs_u=""
    _rs_s="$(slug_of_url "$_rs_u")"
    if slug_valid "$_rs_s"; then printf '%s\n' "$_rs_s"; return 0; fi
    _rs_pin "$_rs_d/../contracts/repo-slug.txt"
  else
    _rs_pin "$_rs_d/repo-slug.txt"
  fi
  return 0
}

# ── the reconcile interface (harbor#1031, contracts/reconcile.md) ────────────
# A drift check's `--status` prints ONE shape on stdout, whoever wrote the check: a header, one record per item
# that is NOT at its desired state (desired, observed, delta, and how long it has been), the items that
# converged since the last run, and a summary. The delta and the ages, never the census.
#   status_init <id> [config-dir]  the header. The id is the check's receipt id; returns 1 when it is not a file name
#   status_ok [count]              items judged and at their desired state: counted, never printed
#   status_drift <key> <desired> <observed> [delta]   an item that is not: `new` the first run it is seen, `standing`
#                                  (with its age in seconds) every run after, until it converges. A key given twice in one
#                                  run is one row (the first), counted once
#   status_unjudged <reason>       the run could not judge: prints `unchecked`, leaves the first-seen state alone, returns 3
#   status_end                     `cleared` for every item gone since the last run, the summary, the state saved;
#                                  returns 0 when nothing drifted and 1 when something did (the caller exits with it)
# The first-seen state is <config dir>/cache/reconcile/<id>.tsv (`key<TAB>epoch`), written only by a run that judged.
# A tool that sources this and sets LOG_FD=2 keeps stdout as data, which a --status caller must.
reconcile_dir() { printf '%s' "${1:-${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}}/cache/reconcile"; }
_st_f() { printf '%s' "${1-}" | tr '\t\n\r' '   '; }   # one field: a tab or a line break would move every column after it
status_init() {
  _ST_ID="${1:-}"; _ST_CFG="${2:-}"; _ST_OPEN=0; _ST_PERSIST=0; _ST_EX=0; _ST_DR=0
  _ST_PREV=""; _ST_NEW=""; _ST_NOW=0
  _ST_SEEN='
'
  case "$_ST_ID" in ''|.*|*..*|*.|*[!abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0-9.-]*) _ST_ID=""; return 1 ;; esac
  printf 'reconcile\t1\t%s\n' "$_ST_ID"
}
# Opened by the first item, not by status_init, so a run that cannot judge needs nothing but printf.
_st_open() {
  [ "$_ST_OPEN" = 0 ] || return 0
  _ST_OPEN=1
  _ST_NOW="$(date +%s 2>/dev/null)"; case "$_ST_NOW" in ''|*[!0-9]*) _ST_NOW=0 ;; esac
  _ST_DIR="$(reconcile_dir "$_ST_CFG")"; _ST_PREV="$_ST_DIR/$_ST_ID.tsv"
  # A config dir that is not there is not made for this: nothing is installed in it, so there is nothing to remember.
  [ -d "${_ST_CFG:-${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}}" ] || { _ST_NEW=""; return 0; }
  if [ "$_ST_NOW" -gt 0 ] && [ -n "$_ST_ID" ] && mkdir -p "$_ST_DIR" 2>/dev/null \
     && _ST_NEW="$(mktemp "$_ST_DIR/.$_ST_ID.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" && [ -n "$_ST_NEW" ]; then
    _ST_PERSIST=1
  else
    _ST_NEW=""; log_warn "reconcile: first-seen state cannot be kept in $_ST_DIR, so ages are unknown this run"
  fi
}
status_ok() { _ST_EX=$((_ST_EX + ${1:-1})); }   # [count]
status_drift() { # <key> <desired> <observed> [delta]
  _sk="$(_st_f "${1-}")"; [ -n "$_sk" ] || _sk='-'
  # A key is unique within a report, and one item can be found by more than one wiring (a script wired under two matchers):
  # the first sighting is the row, and a repeat is neither listed, counted nor remembered a second time.
  case "$_ST_SEEN" in *"
$_sk
"*) return 0 ;; esac
  _ST_SEEN="$_ST_SEEN$_sk
"
  _st_open
  _ST_EX=$((_ST_EX + 1)); _ST_DR=$((_ST_DR + 1))
  _sa='-'; _sy=standing
  if [ "$_ST_PERSIST" = 1 ]; then
    # ENVIRON, not -v: awk reads a backslash in a -v value as an escape, and a key may hold one
    _sf=""; [ ! -f "$_ST_PREV" ] || _sf="$(RECONCILE_K="$_sk" awk -F'\t' '$1 == ENVIRON["RECONCILE_K"] { print $2; exit }' "$_ST_PREV" 2>/dev/null)"
    case "$_sf" in ''|*[!0-9]*) _sf="$_ST_NOW"; _sy=new ;; esac
    _sa=$((_ST_NOW - _sf)); [ "$_sa" -ge 0 ] || _sa=0
    printf '%s\t%s\n' "$_sk" "$_sf" >> "$_ST_NEW"
  fi
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$_sy" "$_sk" "$(_st_f "${2-}")" "$(_st_f "${3-}")" "$(_st_f "${4:--}")" "$_sa"
}
status_unjudged() { # <reason>
  [ -z "${_ST_NEW:-}" ] || rm -f "$_ST_NEW" 2>/dev/null
  printf 'unchecked\t%s\n' "$(_st_f "${1-}")"
  return 3
}
status_end() {
  _st_open
  _sc=0
  if [ "$_ST_PERSIST" = 1 ] && [ -f "$_ST_PREV" ]; then
    # keys the last run held and this one does not: converged (or no longer examined)
    # the new file is read in BEGIN: with NR == FNR an empty new file would leave the old one looking like the first
    RECONCILE_NEW="$_ST_NEW" awk -F'\t' 'BEGIN { while ((getline l < ENVIRON["RECONCILE_NEW"]) > 0) { split(l, a, "\t"); seen[a[1]] = 1 } }
      !($1 in seen) { print $1 }' "$_ST_PREV" > "$_ST_NEW.cl" 2>/dev/null || : > "$_ST_NEW.cl"
    while IFS= read -r _sk; do
      [ -n "$_sk" ] || continue
      printf 'cleared\t%s\n' "$_sk"; _sc=$((_sc + 1))
    done < "$_ST_NEW.cl"
    rm -f "$_ST_NEW.cl" 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf 'summary\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$_ST_EX" "$_ST_DR" "$_sc"
  if [ "$_ST_PERSIST" = 1 ]; then
    mv -f "$_ST_NEW" "$_ST_PREV" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f "$_ST_NEW" 2>/dev/null; log_warn "reconcile: first-seen state was not saved to $_ST_PREV"; }
  fi
  [ "$_ST_DR" -eq 0 ]
}

# ── the auto-remediation allowlist (harbor#1031 item 4) ──────────────────────
# One list says what may repair without a person: the HEAL rows of contracts/finding.md (the lanes block), added by a
# person's PR. A reconciler (a tool that fixes what a drift check found) asks before it repairs, and a repair the rows
# do not name is refused, never run. `--status` itself repairs nothing; this is for the tool that does.
#   heal_rows [contract]                        `lane TAB key TAB subject TAB repair`, one per row of the lanes block
#   repair_allowed <key> <subject> <repair> [contract]   0 when a HEAL row of <key> matches <subject> and <repair> is its repair
#                                               (`<subject>` read as "$1", the way the runner passes it); else 2, a FAIL and a fix
#                                               on the log. <subject> is `-` for a repair that takes none
heal_rows() { # [contract]
  awk '/^<!-- lanes:begin -->$/ { t = 1; next } /^<!-- lanes:end -->$/ { t = 0 } t && /^\|/' "${1:-${ROOT:-.}/contracts/finding.md}" 2>/dev/null \
    | awk -F'|' '{ for (i = 2; i < NF; i++) { f = $i; gsub(/`/, "", f); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", f); $i = f }
                   if ($2 == "lane" || $2 ~ /^-+$/) next
                   printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", $2, $3, $4, $5 }'
}
repair_allowed() { # <key> <subject> <repair> [contract]
  _ra_k="${1-}"; _ra_s="${2-}"; _ra_c="${3-}"; _ra_f="${4:-${ROOT:-.}/contracts/finding.md}"
  [ -f "$_ra_f" ] || { log_fail "repair refused: no allowlist at $_ra_f, so nothing says what may repair"; log_fix "git checkout origin/main -- contracts/finding.md"; return 2; }
  [ "$_ra_s" != stood-down ] || { log_fail "repair refused: $_ra_k is stood down, so a person reads it"; log_nofix "contracts/finding.md, the HEAL rows"; return 2; }
  _ra_rows="$(heal_rows "$_ra_f")"
  while IFS='	' read -r _rl _rk _rs _rr; do
    [ "$_rl" = HEAL ] && [ "$_rk" = "$_ra_k" ] || continue
    [ "$(printf '%s' "$_rr" | sed 's/<subject>/"$1"/g')" = "$_ra_c" ] || continue
    # shellcheck disable=SC2254
    case "$_ra_s" in -) return 0 ;; $_rs) return 0 ;; esac
  done <<RA_ROWS
$_ra_rows
RA_ROWS
  log_fail "repair refused: $_ra_c on ${_ra_s} is not a HEAL row of $_ra_k in contracts/finding.md"
  log_fix "a person adds the row to the lanes block of contracts/finding.md in a PR; nothing else may repair on its own"
  return 2
}

#!/usr/bin/env sh
# lint-name.sh (harbor#950) — the naming lint: judges names against standards/naming/*.tsv and generates its views.
#
#   sh bin/lint-name.sh                           judge every tracked name in the tree
#   sh bin/lint-name.sh --changed                 judge only paths added or changed since the base
#   sh bin/lint-name.sh --added                   judge only the paths the branch ADDS since the base (git diff
#                                                 --diff-filter=A, a rename counting as an add): a name the branch
#                                                 brings in and no legacy row covers; the registry is not re-judged
#   sh bin/lint-name.sh --check <surface> <name>  judge one name; the scaffolder calls this at a name's birth.
#                                                 `path.test` is the test surface under its second name and `case` is
#                                                 path judged for name.case alone (surfaces.tsv, view); `repo-kind`
#                                                 takes a directory: its .agents/config.yaml names the kind, and the
#                                                 entries repo-kinds.tsv requires of it must be there; `overlay` takes a
#                                                 directory and judges the repo overlay at its root (below)
#   sh bin/lint-name.sh --self-test               every fail fixture goes red, every pass stays green, every rule
#                                                 goes red on every surface controls.tsv declares for it, and every
#                                                 grammar surface's example survives parse then render unchanged
#     --rule <id>                                 (repeatable) limit it to those rules: their fail fixtures, the pass fixtures
#                                                 of the surfaces they declare (judged for those rules only) and their
#                                                 coverage, not the other rules, the examples or the full census (harbor#667).
#                                                 Still runs the grammar, register and validator checks. Not a gate: the
#                                                 full self-test stays the default and the one a tree is judged by
#   sh bin/lint-name.sh --render <surface> k=v..  a tuple rendered by surfaces.tsv's grammar, e.g.
#                                                 --render bin family=admission object=bash ext=sh
#   sh bin/lint-name.sh --parse <surface> <name>  a name parsed back into its slots, one k=v per line
#   sh bin/lint-name.sh --gen <view>              glossary | naming-guide | cli-tree | labels | vale | exemptions | vendors |
#                                                 issue-taxonomy,
#                                                 written under build/ (untracked)
#   sh bin/lint-name.sh --list                    every lint rule id, its mode and title: controls.tsv's, then
#                                                 bin/lint-conventions.sh's (harbor#957), one list with no id twice
#   sh bin/lint-name.sh --help
#
#   --format findings   also print one `<A|V> TAB <rule> TAB <subject>` record per finding on stdout
#   --root <dir>        the tree to judge (default: this checkout; a vendored copy judges the repo that carries it)
#   --registry <dir>    the registry (default: <root>/standards/naming; a vendored copy's own registry/ when the root has none).
#                       A root with no standards/naming/ is a workload: the rules that judge the registry itself stay silent (harbor#1415)
#   --base <ref>        the base for --changed, --added and name.exemption-grow (default: $HARBOR_CI_BASE or origin/main)
#   --today YYYY-MM-DD  the date alias and exemption expiry is judged against (default: $HARBOR_LINT_TODAY, else today in UTC, D-51)
#   --exemptions-base <file>   the base exemptions.tsv for name.exemption-grow (default: read from git)
#   HARBOR_SCOPE_PRIVATE=<dir>  the private layer whose terms.tsv overlays client and system terms (D-85; default: $PORT_ROOT/harbor-private)
#   <root>/naming-words.tsv, <root>/naming-families.tsv   the repo overlay (harbor#967): a repo's own words and families,
#                               in words.tsv's and terms.tsv's row shape, read from the judged root and never from a root
#                               that holds standards/naming/ (standards/naming.md §14)
#
#   exit (D-49) 0 pass, warn and shadow findings allowed · 1 a block finding, or a failed self-test · 2 usage · 3 unchecked
#   LINT_REDLOG=<file> appends the id of every rule that goes red, as bin/lint-conventions.sh does.
#   mode (D-29, D-64): block fails the run, warn prints, shadow only records (LINT_REDLOG and the count).
#
# DELIBERATELY ONE FILE (docs/explanation/modularity.md): one POSIX sh + awk program so the scaffolder can
# vendor it into any repo with no toolchain (standards/naming.md §10.2). The awk does the judging;
# the sh around it only collects names and formats. Every rule is a controls.tsv row, every term a
# terms.tsv row and every surface's grammar a surfaces.tsv cell: nothing about the vocabulary or the
# grammar is written here, so changing a term or a renderer changes the result with no edit to this file.
#
# WHY NO INLINE IGNORES. A name the standard does not judge is a row in exemptions.tsv, with a
# kind and a reason. Legacy rows were generated from each rule's own first scan and only shrink;
# rows naming the registry, this file or its fixtures are refused (name.exemption-self) and never
# applied, so the lint cannot be talked out of judging itself.
set -eu

# ${0%/*}, not dirname: a hook runs this (context-rules/user/name-note.sh), and a failed fork would make HERE the cwd (harbor#810).
case "$0" in */*) HERE="${0%/*}" ;; *) HERE=. ;; esac
HERE="$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$HERE" && pwd)"
SELF="$HERE/${0##*/}"
# shellcheck disable=SC2034 # LOG_FD: read by library-log.sh
LOG_FD=2   # stdout carries --check, --format findings and --gen output; the log goes to stderr
. "$HERE/library-log.sh"
log_init lint-name

usage() { awk 'NR < 2 { next } /^# DELIBERATELY/ || !/^#/ { exit } { sub(/^# ?/, ""); print }' "$SELF"; }

ACTION=tree; FORMAT=""; ROOT=""; REG=""; BASE="${HARBOR_CI_BASE:-origin/main}"; TODAY=""; EXBASE=""
RULES=""      # --rule ids, space-terminated; empty = the full self-test
UNCHECKED=3   # D-49: pass 0, fail 1, usage 2, unchecked 3
SURFACE=""; NAME=""; VIEW=""; SLOTS=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    --changed) ACTION=changed ;;
    --added) ACTION=added ;;
    --self-test) ACTION=self-test ;;
    --rule) [ $# -ge 2 ] || { log_fail "--rule needs a rule id"; log_fix "sh $SELF --self-test --rule name.case"; log_end || :; exit 2; }
            RULES="$RULES$2 "; shift ;;
    --list) ACTION=list ;;
    --check) ACTION=check
             [ $# -ge 3 ] || { log_fail "--check needs <surface> <name>"; log_fix "sh $SELF --check path docs/reports/2026-10-03-review.md"; log_end || :; exit 2; }
             SURFACE="$2"; NAME="$3"; shift 2 ;;
    --parse) ACTION=parse
             [ $# -ge 3 ] || { log_fail "--parse needs <surface> <name>"; log_fix "sh $SELF --parse bin admission-bash.sh"; log_end || :; exit 2; }
             SURFACE="$2"; NAME="$3"; shift 2 ;;
    --render) ACTION=render
              [ $# -ge 2 ] || { log_fail "--render needs <surface> and k=v slots"; log_fix "sh $SELF --render bin family=admission object=bash ext=sh"; log_end || :; exit 2; }
              SURFACE="$2"; shift 2
              while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
                case "$1" in -*) break ;; esac
                SLOTS="$SLOTS$1 "; shift
              done
              continue ;;
    --gen) ACTION=gen
           [ $# -ge 2 ] || { log_fail "--gen needs a view"; log_fix "sh $SELF --gen glossary"; log_end || :; exit 2; }
           VIEW="$2"; shift ;;
    --format) [ "${2:-}" = findings ] || { log_fail "--format takes only: findings"; log_fix "sh $SELF --format findings"; log_end || :; exit 2; }
              FORMAT=findings; shift ;;
    --root|--registry|--base|--today|--exemptions-base)
      [ $# -ge 2 ] || { log_fail "$1 needs a value"; log_fix "sh $SELF --help"; log_end || :; exit 2; }
      case "$1" in
        --root) ROOT="$2" ;; --registry) REG="$2" ;; --base) BASE="$2" ;;
        --today) TODAY="$2" ;; --exemptions-base) EXBASE="$2" ;;
      esac; shift ;;
    *) log_fail "unknown argument: $1"; log_fix "sh $SELF --help"; log_end || :; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  shift
done

[ -z "$RULES" ] || [ "$ACTION" = self-test ] || { log_fail "--rule only limits --self-test"; log_fix "sh $SELF --self-test --rule name.case"; log_end || :; exit 2; }

# A vendored copy (vendor/naming/, MANIFEST.tsv beside it) judges the repo that carries it, with the registry beside it
# (harbor#967, #1415): bare, it finds both; harbor's own bin/ has neither file, so its defaults are unchanged.
VENDORED=0; [ ! -f "$HERE/MANIFEST.tsv" ] || [ ! -f "$HERE/registry/registers.tsv" ] || VENDORED=1
if [ "$VENDORED" = 1 ] && [ -z "$ROOT" ]; then ROOT="$HERE/../.."; fi
ROOT="${ROOT:-$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$HERE/.." && pwd)}"
ROOT="$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$ROOT" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || { log_fail "no such root: $ROOT"; log_fix "sh $SELF --root <dir>"; log_end || :; exit 2; }
if [ -z "$REG" ] && [ "$VENDORED" = 1 ] && [ ! -f "$ROOT/standards/naming/registers.tsv" ]; then REG="$HERE/registry"; fi
REG="${REG:-$ROOT/standards/naming}"
TODAY="${TODAY:-${HARBOR_LINT_TODAY:-$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)}}"   # D-51: UTC for every date; the env pins it for a caller that cannot pass --today
case "$TODAY" in [0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]) ;; *)
  log_fail "--today is not YYYY-MM-DD: $TODAY"; log_fix "sh $SELF --today 2026-10-04"; log_end || :; exit 2 ;;
esac
T="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/lint-name.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT INT TERM HUP

# The registry this run reads: --check registry <dir> overlays <dir>/<file> on the registry, so a
# fixture holds only the one file it breaks. A registry that cannot be read is UNCHECKED, never clean.
OVERLAY=""
[ "$ACTION" != check ] || [ "$SURFACE" != registry ] || OVERLAY="$NAME"
# A fixture file that opens with `#` replaces the registry's; one that holds rows only is appended
# below a `# fixture rows` line, so most fixtures are one row and never drift from the registry.
reg_file() { # <file> -> the path this run reads it from
  case "$OVERLAY" in /*) _o="$OVERLAY" ;; '') _o="" ;; *) _o="$ROOT/$OVERLAY" ;; esac
  if [ -z "$_o" ] || [ ! -f "$_o/$1" ]; then printf '%s' "$REG/$1"; return 0; fi
