# surfaces.tsv (harbor#950) — every surface a name is rendered on, and how (standards/naming.md §6.1).
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. One tuple of terms gives every surface its name, so the renderer per
# surface is the grammar's other half. Before this file it was a table in prose that the lint
# could not read; the naming guide is now generated from these rows (`--gen naming-guide`), and
# every example below runs as a pass fixture in `bin/lint-name.sh --self-test`, so an example the
# lint rejects fails the build.
#
# standard_version: 2.0.0
#
# COLUMNS  id <TAB> renderer <TAB> family <TAB> checked <TAB> example <TAB> rule <TAB> view <TAB> note
#   id        the surface id that `bin/lint-name.sh --check <surface> <name>` takes
#   renderer  a GRAMMAR when `rule` is set, prose otherwise. The lint parses a name back through it
#             and renders a tuple with it (`--parse`, `--render`), so editing the cell changes the
#             verdict. <slot> is one word group, [..] is optional, anything else is literal, and a
#             slot spelled in capitals renders in capitals. Slots: <family> <verb> <system> (or
#             <REPO>) are registered terms; <family-or-domain> is a family or a domain; <object>
#             <subject> <aspect> <name> <id> <ext> are free. The joiner inside a slot is _ when the
#             grammar has an _ and - otherwise.
#   family    required | optional | -   whether the first word must be a family (or a domain)
#   checked   tree     lint-name.sh scans the repo tree for it, and --check accepts it
#             check    --check accepts it; nothing in a repo tree carries it
#             no       not machine-checked here: another tool, or review only (the note says which)
#   example   a name that MUST pass; - when the surface is not checked, or when the thing checked is
#             a directory on disk and its examples are the fixtures (repo-kind). Every example whose
#             `rule` is set must also survive parse then render unchanged (--self-test)
#   rule      the rules id that reports a name the grammar does not parse or whose slot is not
#             the registered term it needs; - when the renderer is prose, not a grammar
#   view      - when the surface is judged by its own code. Otherwise <surface>[:<rule>,<rule>]: this
#             id is another surface under a second name (`path.test` is `test`), or that surface
#             judged for the listed rules only (`case` is `path` reporting name.case alone). The
#             target is a row of this file and each rule a row of controls.tsv; a view is never of a view
id	renderer	family	checked	example	rule	view	note

# terms.tsv (harbor#950) — THE ONLY PLACE the controlled vocabulary exists.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A name is a tuple of vocabulary terms rendered once per surface
# (standards/naming.md §0). Before this file the vocabulary lived in prose, in the lint's
# regexes and in each reader's head, so a word could mean two things and nothing noticed.
# bin/lint-name.sh reads this file and nothing else for the term sets, and the glossary,
# naming guide, CLI tree, label set and Vale config are generated from it. Change a term
# here and the lint result and the generated glossary change with no other edit.
#
# standard_version: 2.0.0
#
# SEED. The concept rows come from research/02 §1 (219 concepts, harbor#949), with the
# standard's own classes laid over them: families and verbs (§3), kinds (§4), layers (§5),
# domains, clients and abbreviations (D-18, D-26, D-35), plus two classes the lint needs:
# `system` (a repo name usable as an env prefix, D-15) and `extension` (§6.3's registered
# extension chain), and `subject` (the lint subject families of §3). Every closed set is a
# class here, never prose or code (09a S4): mode, outcome, decision, severity, state (D-29),
# control-type, moment, function, lifecycle (D-62), and level (D-57).
#
# COLUMNS  id <TAB> class <TAB> pref <TAB> broader <TAB> vsm <TAB> stability <TAB> successor
#          <TAB> src <TAB> alt <TAB> depends_on <TAB> definition
#   id          the canonical word: lowercase kebab, a digit never starts a word
#   class       one or more of family verb domain client abbreviation kind layer concept
#               system extension subject level mode outcome decision severity priority state
#               control-type moment function lifecycle share relation modality tier strength commit-type, comma-separated.

# verbs.tsv (harbor#1428) — the task verbs a repo's justfile answers, and which kinds of repo must carry each.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `just test` meant a different thing in every repo, and a scaffolded repo got a verb set
# that its own scaffolder and its controller did not carry (harbor#1428, measured 2026-11-01). One row per verb
# says what it means and what its exit code promises, so the same word means the same thing everywhere; the
# `kinds` cell says which repo-kinds.tsv kinds must have it. `bin/lint-name.sh --check repo-kind <dir>` reads the
# recipe names of <dir>/justfile and reports a required verb it lacks as name.repo-verb; the fleet audit calls it.
# yard renders the verb set of a scaffolded repo's justfile from this file (tools/generate_justfile.py there; a stack's own recipes stay in tools/justfile-recipes/, and a required verb a stack lacks renders as a stub that exits non-zero).
# An exemption is a row in the repo's own naming-exemptions.tsv: rule name.repo-verb, subject repo-verb:<id>.
#
# standard_version: 2.0.0
#
# COLUMNS  id <TAB> meaning <TAB> exit <TAB> kinds <TAB> note
#   id      the recipe name, a bare lowercase kebab word
#   meaning what running it does, one clause
#   exit    what the exit code promises: always 0 = done, non-zero = the thing is not so; a verb that cannot run
#           here says so and exits non-zero (never a silent 0)
#   kinds   space-separated repo-kinds.tsv ids that must carry the verb; - when no kind must (an optional verb
#           the standard still names, so its meaning is the same where it exists)
#   note    why the kinds are the ones they are
id	meaning	exit	kinds	note
setup	install or sync the dependencies a checkout needs	0 ready, non-zero a step failed	scaffolder fleet-controller workload data	the first command in a clean checkout
lint	static checks over the repo, writing nothing	0 clean, non-zero a finding	control-plane scaffolder fleet-controller workload data	every kind
typecheck	the static type check of the project code	0 clean, non-zero a type error	scaffolder fleet-controller workload	-
format	rewrite the project code to the formatter's output	0 done	scaffolder fleet-controller workload	the one verb that writes source
test	the whole suite	0 all pass, non-zero a failure	control-plane scaffolder fleet-controller workload data	every kind
test-quick	the suite, stopping at the first failure	0 all pass, non-zero a failure	scaffolder fleet-controller workload	the edit loop
test-cov	the suite with a coverage report and its floor	0 above the floor, non-zero a failure or below it	-	optional: a stack with no coverage tool has no floor
test-mutation	mutation testing over the core logic	0 survivors within bounds, non-zero above	-	optional: slow, nightly, python stacks
audit	known-vulnerability scan of the dependencies	0 none found, non-zero a finding	scaffolder fleet-controller workload	-
sbom	write a software bill of materials of the runtime dependencies	0 written	scaffolder fleet-controller workload	-
license	dependency license scan	0 compliant, non-zero a denied license	scaffolder fleet-controller workload	-
fuzz	property-based or fuzz tests	0 pass, non-zero a failure	scaffolder fleet-controller workload	nightly, never a PR gate
scan	secret scan of the staged changes	0 clean, non-zero a secret found	scaffolder fleet-controller workload	-
naming	the naming standard ratchet over the repo	0 no new finding, 3 unchecked	scaffolder fleet-controller workload	exit 3 is never a pass
docs	serve or build the docs site	0 done	scaffolder fleet-controller workload	-
ci	everything CI runs, in CI's order	0 CI would pass	scaffolder fleet-controller workload data	the full gate
fast-ci	the local pre-push gate: lint and the suite	0 pass	scaffolder fleet-controller workload	lighter than ci on purpose
ci-local-on	route CI to the self-hosted runner	0 variable set	scaffolder fleet-controller workload	needs gh and a registered runner

# versions.tsv (harbor#1426) — the one register of the runtimes, tools, libraries and GitHub Actions every governed repo pins.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Fourteen repos pinned the same things at different values: requires-python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13, a
# .python-version of 3.14 in a repo that requires 3.11, ruff `>=0.4` beside `>=0.14`, three SHAs of actions/checkout and a mutable
# `@v5` tag in eight places on the path of the one required gate. yard's tools/pinned-third-party.toml already had the right
# semantics (a vetted pin, hold_at with a reason, upgrade-as-PR, never auto-merged) for one tool in one repo; this is that model
# for the box. The drift check (fleet's projects_orchestrator.versions) prints each repo's difference from this file, and a
# difference is either fixed or a row in the repo's exception file with its reason. A pin found in a repo that this file does not
# name is red (standard.version-registered, in the drift check), so a new tool cannot be pinned in only one place.
#

# writers.tsv (harbor#978 item 8) — every script that CREATES a named thing, and the command patterns that find them.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A writer that builds a branch, issue title or PR title by hand is a second copy of the
# grammar, and it drifts while reading correctly. `bin/lint-renderer.sh` (rule name.renderer-used) holds each
# `writer` row to calling the renderer (`lint-name.sh --render`), and scans bin/ and hooks/ for the `pattern`
# rows so a writer missing from this census is itself a finding. Workload writers are registered by their pack.
#
# standard_version: 2.0.0
#
# COLUMNS  id <TAB> kind <TAB> value <TAB> surface <TAB> note
#   kind     writer (value: a repo-relative file) or pattern (value: an ERE a creating command line matches)
#   surface  the surface in surfaces.tsv the written name is judged as
id	kind	value	surface	note
branch-create	pattern	git( -C [^ ]+)? (worktree add -b|checkout -b|switch -c) 	branch	a command that creates a branch
issue-create	pattern	gh issue create 	issue-title	a command that opens an issue
pr-create	pattern	gh pr create 	commit	a command that opens a PR; its title is a commit subject
worktree-sh	writer	bin/worktree.sh	branch	worktree.sh new <branch>
findings-sh	writer	bin/lint-findings.sh	issue-title	finding issues and heal PRs
ci-runs-on-sh	writer	bin/ci-runs-on.sh	branch	the runs-on adoption branch and PR
vendor/naming/standard-vendor.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env sh
# standard-vendor.sh (harbor#967 item 4, decision harbor#1002) — vendors the naming package into a repo.
#
#   sh bin/standard-vendor.sh <repo>            write <repo>/vendor/naming/: lint-name.sh, lint-renderer.sh, standard-register.sh, library-log.sh,
#                                               registry/*.tsv and MANIFEST.tsv (header + one row per file)
#   sh bin/standard-vendor.sh --check <repo>    report drift from harbor; writes nothing
#   sh vendor/naming/standard-vendor.sh --check --offline <repo>
#                                               a workload's CI, with no harbor: every vendored file against its own
#                                               manifest row (edited, missing, extra); no stale or version judgement
#   options: --source <dir> (the harbor tree to vendor from; default this checkout)
#   exit 0 written / current · 1 drift (stale, edited, missing or extra file) · 2 usage · 3 unchecked (no manifest, no source)
# This file ships in the package (harbor#967): the workload's own copy is what its CI runs, offline.
#
# The vendored lint runs offline and needs no flags: bare, it judges the repo that carries it with the registry beside it
# (workload names only, harbor#1415); a name at its birth: sh vendor/naming/lint-name.sh --check <surface> <name>
# MANIFEST.tsv opens with `#` header lines (generated, harbor commit, standard_version) then `path sha256 source` rows.
# --check says three different things: `stale` (the manifest differs from harbor now: upgrade), `edited` (the file differs
# from its own manifest row: someone edited a generated layer) and `missing`/`extra`. The harbor commit is the pin the
# fleet reads for lag; drift itself is judged on content, never on the commit, so vendoring into harbor does not chase its own HEAD.
set -eu
LC_ALL=C; export LC_ALL
case "$0" in */*) SRC="${0%/*}" ;; *) SRC=. ;; esac
SRC="$(CDPATH= cd -- "$SRC" && pwd -P)"
. "$SRC/library-log.sh"
# shellcheck disable=SC2034 # LOG_FD: read by library-log.sh
LOG_FD=2; log_init standard-vendor

usage() { awk 'NR < 2 { next } !/^#/ { exit } { sub(/^# ?/, ""); print }' "$SRC/standard-vendor.sh"; }
die2() { log_fail "$1"; log_fix "$2"; log_end || :; exit 2; }

MODE=write; OFFLINE=0; REPO=""; HSRC="$(CDPATH= cd -- "$SRC/.." && pwd -P)"
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    --check) MODE=check ;;
    --offline) OFFLINE=1 ;;
    --source) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die2 "--source wants a directory" "sh $SRC/standard-vendor.sh --source ~/port/harbor <repo>"; HSRC="$2"; shift ;;
    -*) die2 "unknown flag: $1" "sh $SRC/standard-vendor.sh --help" ;;
    *) [ -z "$REPO" ] || die2 "one repo at a time" "sh $SRC/standard-vendor.sh <repo>"; REPO="$1" ;;
  esac
  shift
done
[ -n "$REPO" ] || die2 "no repo given" "sh $SRC/standard-vendor.sh <repo-path>"
[ -d "$REPO" ] || die2 "no such directory: $REPO" "sh $SRC/standard-vendor.sh <an existing repo>"
HSRC="$(CDPATH= cd -- "$HSRC" && pwd -P)"; REPO="$(CDPATH= cd -- "$REPO" && pwd -P)"
DEST="$REPO/vendor/naming"; MAN="$DEST/MANIFEST.tsv"
[ "$OFFLINE" = 0 ] || [ "$MODE" = check ] || die2 "--offline only checks: writing needs a harbor tree" "sh <a harbor checkout>/bin/standard-vendor.sh $REPO"

if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha() { shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -c1-64; }; else sha() { sha256sum "$1" | cut -c1-64; }; fi

# The package: <path under vendor/naming> TAB <source path under the harbor tree>, one per line. The kit manifest
# (standards/naming/kit.tsv, harbor#1436) names it: its vendored=yes tool and register rows, so "yard vendors it" is one list.
# A tree without the manifest (an older harbor) is vendored the way it was: the fixed tools and every standards/naming/*.tsv.
package() {
  if [ -f "$HSRC/standards/naming/kit.tsv" ]; then
    sh "$HSRC/bin/standard-kit.sh" --root "$HSRC" --registry "$HSRC/standards/naming" --package; return
  fi
  printf 'lint-name.sh\tbin/lint-name.sh\nlint-renderer.sh\tbin/lint-renderer.sh\nlibrary-log.sh\tbin/library-log.sh\n'
  printf 'standard-vendor.sh\tbin/standard-vendor.sh\nstandard-register.sh\tbin/standard-register.sh\n'
  printf 'doc-shape.sh\tbin/doc-shape.sh\ndoc-fresh-verify.sh\tbin/doc-fresh-verify.sh\n'   # harbor#1434, #1435
  for _f in "$HSRC"/standards/naming/*.tsv; do
    [ -f "$_f" ] || continue
    printf 'registry/%s\tstandards/naming/%s\n' "${_f##*/}" "${_f##*/}"
  done
}
[ "$OFFLINE" = 1 ] || for _need in bin/lint-name.sh bin/lint-renderer.sh bin/library-log.sh bin/standard-vendor.sh bin/standard-register.sh bin/doc-shape.sh bin/doc-fresh-verify.sh bin/standard-kit.sh standards/naming/registers.tsv; do
  [ -f "$HSRC/$_need" ] || { log_fail "no $_need under $HSRC (unchecked)"; log_fix "sh $SRC/standard-vendor.sh --source <a harbor checkout> $REPO"; log_end || :; exit 3; }
done
SV="$(sed -n 's/^# standard_version: *//p' "$HSRC/standards/naming/registers.tsv" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)" || SV=""
[ -n "$SV" ] || [ "$OFFLINE" = 1 ] || { log_fail "registers.tsv carries no standard_version (unchecked)"; log_fix "restore the '# standard_version:' line in $HSRC/standards/naming/registers.tsv"; log_end || :; exit 3; }
COMMIT="$(git -C "$HSRC" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"

if [ "$MODE" = write ]; then
  rm -rf "$DEST.new"; mkdir -p "$DEST.new/registry"
  {
    # harbor's own row says the repo-relative command; any other repo's row names the checkout it is run from (harbor#1434)
    if [ "$REPO" = "$HSRC" ]; then printf '# generated-by: sh bin/standard-vendor.sh .\n'; else printf '# generated-by: sh <standard checkout>/bin/standard-vendor.sh .\n'; fi
    printf '# MANIFEST.tsv — GENERATED by bin/standard-vendor.sh, do not edit: re-run it (harbor#967, #1002).\n'
    printf '# harbor_commit: %s\n# standard_version: %s\n# columns: path\tsha256\tsource\n' "$COMMIT" "$SV"
    package | while IFS="$(printf '\t')" read -r _p _s; do
      cp "$HSRC/$_s" "$DEST.new/$_p"
      printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$_p" "$(sha "$DEST.new/$_p")" "$_s"
    done
  } > "$DEST.new/MANIFEST.tsv"
  chmod +x "$DEST.new/lint-name.sh" "$DEST.new/lint-renderer.sh" "$DEST.new/standard-vendor.sh" "$DEST.new/standard-register.sh" "$DEST.new/standard-kit.sh" 2>/dev/null || :
  rm -rf "$DEST"; mkdir -p "$REPO/vendor"; mv "$DEST.new" "$DEST"
  _n="$(grep -vc '^#' "$MAN")"
  log_ok "vendored naming@$SV ($_n files) from harbor ${COMMIT%"${COMMIT#???????}"} into $DEST"
  log_end || :; exit 0
fi

# --check
[ -f "$MAN" ] || { log_fail "no $MAN: nothing is vendored here (unchecked)"; log_fix "sh $SRC/standard-vendor.sh $REPO"; log_end || :; exit 3; }
PIN="$(sed -n 's/^# harbor_commit: *//p' "$MAN" | head -n 1)"; PINV="$(sed -n 's/^# standard_version: *//p' "$MAN" | head -n 1)"
DRIFT=0
if [ "$OFFLINE" = 1 ]; then REFIX="re-vendor from harbor: sh <a harbor checkout>/bin/standard-vendor.sh $REPO"; else REFIX="sh $SRC/standard-vendor.sh $REPO"; fi
bad() { DRIFT=$((DRIFT + 1)); log_fail "$1"; log_fix "$REFIX"; }
TAB="$(printf '\t')"
# Every manifest row against the file on disk (edited, missing) and against harbor now (stale).
grep -v '^#' "$MAN" | { while IFS="$TAB" read -r _p _h _s; do
    [ -f "$DEST/$_p" ] || { echo "missing $_p"; continue; }
    [ "$(sha "$DEST/$_p")" = "$_h" ] || echo "edited $_p"
    [ "$OFFLINE" = 1 ] && continue
    if [ -f "$HSRC/$_s" ]; then [ "$(sha "$HSRC/$_s")" = "$_h" ] || echo "stale $_p"; else echo "stale $_p (gone from harbor)"; fi
  done
  # A file harbor now ships that the manifest lacks, and a vendored file no row names.
  [ "$OFFLINE" = 1 ] || package | while IFS="$TAB" read -r _p _s; do grep -q "^$_p$TAB" "$MAN" || echo "new $_p"; done
  (cd "$DEST" && find . -type f ! -name MANIFEST.tsv | sed 's|^\./||') | while read -r _p; do
    grep -q "^$_p$TAB" "$MAN" || echo "extra $_p"; done
} > "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/standard-vendor.$$" || :
while read -r _k _rest; do bad "$_k: vendor/naming/$_rest"; done < "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/standard-vendor.$$"
rm -f "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/standard-vendor.$$"
[ "$OFFLINE" = 1 ] || [ "$PINV" = "$SV" ] || bad "standard_version: pinned $PINV, harbor is at $SV"
if [ "$DRIFT" -eq 0 ] && [ "$OFFLINE" = 1 ]; then
  log_ok "naming@$PINV: every vendored file matches its manifest row (offline; currency with harbor not judged)"; log_end || :; exit 0
fi
if [ "$DRIFT" -eq 0 ]; then
  log_ok "naming@$PINV is current with harbor (pinned at ${PIN%"${PIN#???????}"})"; log_end || :; exit 0
fi
log_note "pinned at ${PIN%"${PIN#???????}"}; $DRIFT drift finding(s)" 2>/dev/null || :
log_end || :; exit 1
